weeks.title: Numbers, functions and straight lines
weeks.summary: Is week aap number systems, intervals aur absolute value, function ka domain-range-composition-inverse, aur straight line ki equations seekhoge — sab kuch jo aage calculus aur circuits me roz use hoga.
concepts: **Number systems**: ℕ (1, 2, 3, ...) ⊂ ℤ (integers) ⊂ ℚ (p/q, q ≠ 0) ⊂ ℝ. Rational number ka decimal ya to terminate hota hai ya repeat; √2, π, e jaise irrational numbers ka decimal na rukta hai na repeat hota hai.

**Intervals aur absolute value**: [a, b] me endpoints shaamil, (a, b) me nahi. |x| = distance of x from 0. |x − a| < δ ka matlab a − δ < x < a + δ, yaani a ke aas-paas δ chaudi khidki. Tolerance wale resistor (1 kΩ ± 5%) ko bhi aise likhte hain: |R − 1000| ≤ 50.

**Function**: har input x ko exactly ek output f(x) dena. **Domain** = jin x par formula meaningful hai (denominator ≠ 0, √ ke andar ≥ 0, log ke andar > 0). **Range** = jo outputs actually aate hain. Graph ke liye vertical line test: koi bhi vertical line graph ko ek se zyada baar na kaate.

**Composition aur inverse**: (f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)) — pehle g, phir f; order badalne se answer badal jaata hai. Inverse f⁻¹ sirf one-one function ka hota hai: y = f(x) likho, x ko y me solve karo, phir naam badal do. Graph y = x line me mirror ho jaata hai.

**Slope**: do points (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂) se m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = rise/run. Physical meaning: ek variable doosre ke saath kitni tezi se badalta hai. Ohm's law V = IR me V–I graph ki slope hi resistance R hai.
**Line ki equations**: slope-intercept y = mx + c; point-slope y − y₁ = m(x − x₁); general form ax + by + c = 0 jisme slope = −a/b. Vertical line x = k ki slope defined nahi hoti.
**Parallel aur perpendicular**: parallel lines ki slopes barabar (m₁ = m₂). Perpendicular lines ke liye m₁·m₂ = −1, yaani slope ko ulta karo aur sign badlo: 2/3 ka perpendicular −3/2 hai.

example.problem: Ek temperature sensor ka output linear hai: 20 °C par 1.2 V aur 70 °C par 2.2 V. Output V ko temperature T ke function ki tarah likho, aur batao kis temperature par output 1.8 V hoga.
steps: Answer: **V = 0.02T + 0.8**, aur **T = 50 °C** par output 1.8 V hoga.

mistakes: Perpendicular slope nikalte waqt sirf reciprocal lena aur sign na badalna. 2/3 ka perpendicular 3/2 nahi, −3/2 hai; check karo ki m₁·m₂ = −1 aa raha hai.
Domain me sirf ek condition dekhna. √(x − 2)/(x − 5) jaise function me √ wali condition (x ≥ 2) aur denominator wali condition (x ≠ 5) dono lagani padti hain.
f(g(x)) aur g(f(x)) ko same samajhna. Composition me andar wala function pehle chalta hai; dono order alag-alag nikal ke dekho.
revision: |x − a| ≤ δ ⇔ a − δ ≤ x ≤ a + δ.
Domain: denominator ≠ 0, √ ke andar ≥ 0, log ke andar > 0.
(f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)); inverse ke liye x aur y swap karke solve karo.
Slope m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁); line: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).

questions.question: |2x − 3| ≤ 5 ko satisfy karne wale saare real x ka set kya hai?
questions.explanation: |2x − 3| ≤ 5 ka matlab −5 ≤ 2x − 3 ≤ 5. Teeno taraf 3 jodo: −2 ≤ 2x ≤ 8, phir 2 se divide: −1 ≤ x ≤ 4. (−∞, −1] ∪ [4, ∞) to |2x − 3| ≥ 5 ka answer hai — inequality ki direction ulti padhne ka trap.

questions.question: f(x) = √(x − 2)/(x − 5) ka domain kya hai?
questions.explanation: √ ke andar x − 2 ≥ 0 chahiye, to x ≥ 2 (x = 2 allowed, kyunki √0 = 0). Denominator x − 5 ≠ 0, to x ≠ 5. Dono milake [2, 5) ∪ (5, ∞). [2, ∞) me x = 5 hatana bhool gaye, aur (2, 5) ∪ (5, ∞) me x = 2 bina wajah hata diya.

questions.question: Point (1, 2) se guzarne wali wo line kaunsi hai jo 2x + 3y = 6 ke perpendicular hai?
questions.explanation: 2x + 3y = 6 ki slope −2/3 hai, to perpendicular slope 3/2. y − 2 = (3/2)(x − 1) ⇒ 2y − 4 = 3x − 3 ⇒ 3x − 2y + 1 = 0. 2x + 3y − 8 = 0 parallel line hai, aur 3x + 2y − 7 = 0 ki slope −3/2 hai — reciprocal liya par sign nahi badla.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x + 1 aur g(x) = x² − 3 hain. (f∘g)(2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: (f∘g)(2) = f(g(2)). Pehle g(2) = 4 − 3 = 1, phir f(1) = 2 + 1 = 3. 22 to (g∘f)(2) = g(5) hai — order ulta karne ka trap. 1 sirf g(2) hai, aur 5 sirf f(2).

questions.question: Ek linear sensor 0 °C par 0.5 V aur 100 °C par 4.5 V deta hai. Output 2.1 V ho to temperature kya hai?
questions.explanation: Slope = (4.5 − 0.5)/100 = 0.04 V/°C, to V = 0.5 + 0.04T. 2.1 = 0.5 + 0.04T ⇒ T = 1.6/0.04 = 40 °C. 52.5 °C tab aata hai jab 0.5 V ka offset bhool kar 2.1/0.04 karo; 46.7 °C me line ko origin se guzarta maan liya (2.1/4.5 × 100).

questions.question: f(x) = (x + 1)/(x − 2), x ≠ 2. Iska inverse f⁻¹(x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: y = (x + 1)/(x − 2) ⇒ yx − 2y = x + 1 ⇒ x(y − 1) = 2y + 1 ⇒ x = (2y + 1)/(y − 1). Naam badlo: f⁻¹(x) = (2x + 1)/(x − 1). Check: f(3) = 4 aur f⁻¹(4) = 9/3 = 3 ✓. (x − 2)/(x + 1) sirf 1/f(x) hai — inverse ko reciprocal samajhne ka trap. Isse ye bhi pata chalta hai ki f ki range me 1 nahi aata.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa number irrational hai?
questions.explanation: √12 = 2√3, aur 12 perfect square nahi hai, isliye iska decimal na rukta hai na repeat hota hai — irrational. 0.375 = 3/8 terminate hota hai aur 2.111... = 19/9 repeat hota hai, dono rational. √49 = 7 ek integer hai — har √ ko irrational maan lena yahan ka trap hai.

questions.question: Points (1, 4) aur (3, −2) se guzarne wali line ki slope kya hai?
questions.explanation: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = (−2 − 4)/(3 − 1) = −6/2 = −3. Line neeche ja rahi hai, to slope negative hi honi chahiye. 3 tab aata hai jab upar ek order aur neeche doosra order le lo; −1/3 run/rise (ulta ratio) lene ka trap hai.

questions.question: Ek resistor 470 Ω ± 10% rated hai, yaani |R − 470| ≤ 47. R ki possible values ka interval kya hai?
questions.explanation: |R − 470| ≤ 47 ⇔ −47 ≤ R − 470 ≤ 47 ⇔ 423 ≤ R ≤ 517. Sign ≤ hai, isliye endpoints shaamil — closed interval [423, 517]. (423, 517) endpoints chhod deta hai; [460, 480] 10% ko 10 Ω samajhne ka trap hai; [470, 517] sirf + wali side leta hai.

questions.question: f(x) = x + 2 aur g(x) = 3x² hain. (f∘g)(1) aur (g∘f)(1) kramshah kya hain?
questions.explanation: (f∘g)(1) = f(g(1)) = f(3) = 5. (g∘f)(1) = g(f(1)) = g(3) = 3·9 = 27. Dono alag hain — composition me order matter karta hai. '27 aur 5' order ulta padhne ka trap hai; 11 tab aata hai jab g(1) = (3·1)² = 9 le lo; 9 tab jab g(3) me square bhool kar 3·3 kar do.

questions.question: f(x) = ln(4 − x²) ka domain kya hai?
questions.explanation: Log ke andar strictly positive chahiye: 4 − x² > 0 ⇔ x² < 4 ⇔ −2 < x < 2. x = ±2 par ln 0 undefined hai, isliye [−2, 2] galat hai. (−∞, −2) ∪ (2, ∞) inequality ulti karne se aata hai, aur (0, 2) 'log me x > 0' wali condition ko x par laga dene ka trap hai — condition poore andar wale expression par lagti hai.

questions.question: k ki kis value par lines 2x + ky = 5 aur (k − 1)x + 3y = 2 ek doosre ke perpendicular hongi?
questions.explanation: Slopes: m₁ = −2/k, m₂ = −(k − 1)/3. Perpendicular ⇒ m₁·m₂ = −1 ⇒ 2(k − 1)/(3k) = −1 ⇒ 2k − 2 = −3k ⇒ k = 2/5. Check: k = 2/5 par slopes −5 aur 1/5, product −1 ✓. '3 ya −2' parallel wali condition (2·3 = k(k − 1)) ka answer hai — parallel aur perpendicular mix karne ka trap; −2/5 bracket kholte waqt 2(k − 1) ko 2k + 2 likhne se aata hai.

questions.question: f(x) = x² − 4x + 7, domain [2, ∞), one-one hai. Iska inverse f⁻¹(x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Square complete karo: y = (x − 2)² + 3, to range [3, ∞). (x − 2)² = y − 3 ⇒ x − 2 = ±√(y − 3). Domain x ≥ 2 hai, isliye + sign: x = 2 + √(y − 3). Naam badlo: f⁻¹(x) = 2 + √(x − 3), x ≥ 3. Check: f(5) = 12 aur f⁻¹(12) = 2 + 3 = 5 ✓. − wala root x ≤ 2 wali branch ka inverse hai; √(x − 3) − 2 aur √(x + 3) square complete karte waqt sign ki galti se aate hain.

questions.question: Wo line kaunsi hai jo x + y = 5 aur 2x − y = 1 ke intersection point se guzarti hai aur 3x + 4y = 0 ke parallel hai?
questions.explanation: Dono equations jodo: 3x = 6 ⇒ x = 2, phir y = 3. Parallel line ka form 3x + 4y = c (same a, b, isliye same slope −3/4). (2, 3) rakho: c = 6 + 12 = 18. 4x − 3y = −1 bhi (2, 3) se guzarti hai par perpendicular hai — parallel/perpendicular mix karne ka trap. 3x − 4y = −6 slope ka sign badal deta hai, aur 3x + 4y = 0 is point se guzarti hi nahi.

questions.question: |x − 1| + |x − 4| < 5 ko satisfy karne wale saare real x ka set kya hai?
questions.explanation: Teen regions lo. x ≥ 4: (x − 1) + (x − 4) = 2x − 5 < 5 ⇒ x < 5, to [4, 5). 1 ≤ x < 4: (x − 1) + (4 − x) = 3 < 5 hamesha sach, to poora [1, 4). x < 1: (1 − x) + (4 − x) = 5 − 2x < 5 ⇒ x > 0, to (0, 1). Milake (0, 5). [0, 5] strict < ko ≤ samajhne ka trap hai; [1, 4] sirf beech wala region hai, aur (−∞, 0) ∪ (5, ∞) ulti inequality (> 5) ka set hai.

weeks.title: Linear systems and Gaussian elimination
weeks.summary: Is week aap do variables wale systems ko geometry se samjhoge, phir kisi bhi m equations aur n unknowns wale system ko matrix form aur Gaussian elimination se solve karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Do variables, teen possibilities**: har equation ax + by = c ek line hai. Lines ek point par kaatein to **unique solution**, parallel hon to **no solution**, ek hi line hon to **infinitely many** solutions. Do solutions exactly kabhi nahi hote.

**Determinant test (2×2)**: a₁x + b₁y = c₁, a₂x + b₂y = c₂ ke liye D = a₁b₂ − a₂b₁. D ≠ 0 ⇒ unique solution (Cramer: x = (c₁b₂ − c₂b₁)/D, y = (a₁c₂ − a₂c₁)/D). D = 0 ho to ya to koi solution nahi ya infinite — constants dekh ke decide karo.

**Matrix form**: system ko Ax = b likhte hain — A coefficient matrix (m × n), x unknowns ka column, b right-hand side. Calculation ke liye **augmented matrix** [A | b] banate hain. Circuit ke KCL/KVL equations bhi isi form me aate hain.

**Elementary row operations**: (1) do rows swap karo, (2) kisi row ko non-zero number se multiply karo, (3) ek row me doosri row ka multiple jodo. Inse solution set nahi badalta — yahi elimination ki neev hai.

**Gaussian elimination**: row operations se matrix ko **row echelon form** me lao — har non-zero row ka pehla non-zero entry (**pivot**) upar wali row ke pivot se right me ho, aur zero rows neeche. Phir neeche se upar **back substitution** karo.

**Consistency padhna**: echelon form me agar koi row [0 0 ... 0 | k] ho jisme k ≠ 0, to system inconsistent (no solution). Warna consistent: pivots ki ginti r hai to **free variables = n − r**. r = n ⇒ unique, r < n ⇒ infinitely many.

**Homogeneous system** Ax = 0 hamesha consistent hai (x = 0 to solution hai hi). Agar unknowns equations se zyada hon (n > m), to pivots ≤ m < n, isliye free variable zaroor hoga aur non-zero solutions bhi milenge.

example.problem: Solve karo: x + y + z = 6, 2x + y − z = 1, x − y + 2z = 5.
steps: Augmented matrix likho (neeche code block me).
R₃ → R₃ − 2R₂: [0, 0, 7 | 21]. Ab matrix row echelon form me hai, teen pivots hain, to unique solution.

mistakes: Row operation karte waqt right-hand side (augmented column) ko update karna bhool jaana. Poori row par operation hota hai, | ke baad wala number bhi.
Zero row [0 0 0 | 0] dekh kar 'no solution' bol dena. Ye row sirf batati hai ki ek equation redundant thi; no solution tab hota hai jab [0 0 0 | k] me k ≠ 0 ho.
D = 0 aate hi 'infinitely many' maan lena. D = 0 ka matlab sirf 'unique nahi'; constants check karo — lines parallel bhi ho sakti hain.
revision: Linear system ke solutions: 0, 1 ya infinitely many — kabhi 2 nahi.
Row ops: swap, scale (non-zero), add multiple of another row.
Homogeneous system with n > m ⇒ infinitely many solutions.

questions.question: System 2x + 3y = 7 aur 4x + 6y = 14 ke kitne solutions hain?
questions.explanation: Doosri equation pehli ka exactly 2 guna hai (4x + 6y = 14), to dono ek hi line hain — har point dono ko satisfy karta hai, isliye infinitely many. D = 12 − 12 = 0 dekh kar 'koi nahi' bolna trap hai; constants bhi same ratio me hain, isliye lines parallel nahi, coincident hain.

questions.question: k ki kis value par system x + ky = 3, 2x + 4y = 5 ka koi solution nahi hoga?
questions.explanation: D = 1·4 − 2·k = 4 − 2k = 0 ⇒ k = 2. k = 2 par equations x + 2y = 3 aur x + 2y = 2.5 ban jaati hain — same left side, alag right side, to parallel lines aur koi solution nahi. −2 sign galat lene se aata hai, aur 1/2 tab jab D ko k·4 − 2 likh do.

questions.question: Teen unknowns (x, y, z) wale system ka augmented matrix elimination ke baad neeche diya hai. Solution set ke baare me kya sahi hai?
questions.explanation: Koi row [0 0 0 | k] with k ≠ 0 nahi hai, to system consistent hai. Pivots do hain (x aur y ke columns me), unknowns 3, to free variables = 3 − 2 = 1 (z). Isliye infinitely many solutions. Zero row ko 'no solution' samajhna sabse common trap hai.

questions.question: Ek do-loop circuit ke KVL equations (current ampere me) hain: 5I₁ − 2I₂ = 4 aur −2I₁ + 6I₂ = 1. I₁ aur I₂ kya hain?
questions.explanation: D = 5·6 − (−2)(−2) = 30 − 4 = 26. I₁ = (4·6 − (−2)·1)/26 = 26/26 = 1 A, I₂ = (5·1 − (−2)·4)/26 = 13/26 = 0.5 A. Check: 5 − 1 = 4 ✓, −2 + 3 = 1 ✓. I₁ = 0.8 A, I₂ = 0 sirf pehli equation satisfy karta hai, aur 0.85/−0.12 wala answer −2 ke minus signs gira dene se aata hai.

questions.question: 3 equations aur 4 unknowns wale ek homogeneous system Ax = 0 ke baare me kya hamesha sahi hai?
options: Iska sirf trivial solution x = 0 hai
Iska koi solution na ho, aisa ho sakta hai
Iska exactly ek non-zero solution hai
questions.explanation: Homogeneous system me x = 0 hamesha solution hai, to 'no solution' possible hi nahi. Pivots zyada se zyada 3 (rows ki ginti) ho sakte hain, unknowns 4 hain, to kam se kam 1 free variable bachega — isliye infinitely many solutions. 'Sirf trivial' tab hota jab pivots = unknowns hote.

questions.question: System x + y + z = 1, x + 2y + 3z = 2, x + 3y + az = b. a aur b ki kis value par iske infinitely many solutions honge?
questions.explanation: R₂ − R₁: [0, 1, 2 | 1]. R₃ − R₁: [0, 2, a − 1 | b − 1]. Phir R₃ − 2R₂: [0, 0, a − 5 | b − 3]. a ≠ 5 ⇒ teen pivots, unique solution. a = 5, b ≠ 3 ⇒ [0 0 0 | non-zero], no solution. a = 5, b = 3 ⇒ zero row, ek free variable, infinitely many. 'a = 5, b ≠ 3' wala option no-solution case hai — wahi sabse tempting trap hai.

questions.question: System 3x + 2y = 7 aur 6x + 4y = 10 ke liye determinant D kya hai aur conclusion kya hai?
questions.explanation: D = a₁b₂ − a₂b₁ = 3·4 − 6·2 = 0, to unique solution nahi. Pehli equation ko 2 se multiply karo: 6x + 4y = 14, jabki doosri kehti hai 6x + 4y = 10 — same left side, alag right side, yaani parallel lines. Isliye koi solution nahi. 'D = 0 ⇒ infinitely many' maan lena yahan ka main trap hai; 24 tab aata hai jab minus ki jagah plus laga do.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa elementary row operation NAHI hai?
questions.explanation: Allowed operations: rows swap karna, row ko non-zero number se multiply karna, aur ek row me doosri ka multiple jodna. R₂ → 0·R₂ poori equation mita deta hai aur ise undo nahi kar sakte, isliye solution set badal sakta hai — ye allowed nahi. R₃ → 5R₃ allowed hai kyunki 5 ≠ 0; R₂ − 3R₁ aur swap to elimination ke roz ke steps hain.

questions.question: System x − 2y = 4, 3x + y = 5 ka augmented matrix kya hai? (; rows ko alag karta hai)
questions.explanation: Har equation ek row banti hai: pehle x aur y ke coefficients, phir | ke baad right-hand side. x − 2y = 4 ⇒ [1 −2 | 4], 3x + y = 5 ⇒ [3 1 | 5]. [1 2 | ...] me −2 ka minus sign chhoot gaya; [1 −2 | 5; ...] me right-hand sides adla-badli ho gaye; [1 3 | 4; −2 1 | 5] coefficients ko column-wise (transpose) likhne ka trap hai.

questions.question: Teen unknowns (x, y, z) wale system ka augmented matrix elimination ke baad neeche diya hai. Back substitution se (x, y, z) kya milta hai?
questions.explanation: Neeche se shuru karo: 2z = 4 ⇒ z = 2. Doosri row: y + 3z = 8 ⇒ y = 8 − 6 = 2. Pehli row: x + y + 2z = 9 ⇒ x = 9 − 2 − 4 = 3. (5, 2, 2) tab aata hai jab pehli row me z ka coefficient 2 bhool jao; (−9, 14, 2) me y = 8 + 6 jaisa sign error hua; (2, 2, 3) values ko galat order me likhna hai.

questions.question: 5 unknowns wale ek consistent system ke row echelon form me 3 pivots hain. Free variables kitne hain aur solution set kaisa hai?
questions.explanation: Free variables = n − r = 5 − 3 = 2. System consistent diya hai aur r < n, isliye infinitely many solutions (do parameters wale). '3 free' pivots ki ginti ko hi free variables samajh lena hai; 'koi solution nahi' consistent wali baat ke ulta hai — free variables kabhi inconsistency nahi banate; 'unique' sirf r = n par hota hai.

questions.question: k ki kis value par homogeneous system x + 2y + z = 0, 2x + y + 3z = 0, x − y + kz = 0 ke non-trivial (x = 0 ke alawa) solutions honge?
questions.explanation: Elimination: R₂ − 2R₁ ⇒ [0 −3 1], R₃ − R₁ ⇒ [0 −3 k − 1]. Phir R₃ − R₂ ⇒ [0 0 k − 2]. Agar k ≠ 2 to teen pivots, sirf x = 0. k = 2 par teesri row zero ho jaati hai, ek free variable bachta hai aur non-zero solutions milte hain. (Determinant −3k + 6 = 0 se bhi yahi.) 'Kisi bhi k par nahi' homogeneous system ko hamesha sirf trivial maan lene ka trap hai; k = −2 aakhri step me sign ki galti hai.

questions.question: System x + 2y − z = 1, 2x + 5y + z = 4, x + 3y + 2z = 3 ko solve karo (z = t lo).
questions.explanation: R₂ − 2R₁ ⇒ [0 1 3 | 2], R₃ − R₁ ⇒ [0 1 3 | 2]. R₃ − R₂ ⇒ [0 0 0 | 0], to system consistent hai aur ek free variable z = t. y = 2 − 3t. Pehli row: x = 1 − 2y + z = 1 − 4 + 6t + t = −3 + 7t. Check t = 1: (4, −1, 1) teeno equations satisfy karta hai ✓. −3 + 5t me +z ko −z le liya; 'sirf x = −3, y = 2, z = 0' free variable ko 0 par fix kar deta hai; zero row ko 'no solution' samajhna purana trap hai.

questions.question: k ki kis value par system kx + 2y = 4, 8x + ky = 8 ke infinitely many solutions honge?
questions.explanation: D = k² − 16 = 0 ⇒ k = ±4; inhi par solution unique nahi hota. k = 4: 4x + 2y = 4 aur 8x + 4y = 8 — doosri equation pehli ki exactly double hai, to ek hi line, infinitely many. k = −4: −4x + 2y = 4 aur 8x − 4y = 8; doosri ko −1/2 se multiply karo to −4x + 2y = −4 ≠ 4, parallel lines, koi solution nahi. 'Dono' D = 0 ko seedha infinite samajhne ka trap hai; k ≠ ±4 to unique solution wala case hai.

questions.question: Ek circuit ke equations hain: I₁ + I₂ − I₃ = 0 (KCL), 4I₁ + 2I₃ = 14 aur 3I₂ + 2I₃ = 9 (KVL), current ampere me. I₃ kitna hai?
questions.explanation: KVL se I₁ = (14 − 2I₃)/4 aur I₂ = (9 − 2I₃)/3. KCL me rakho: (14 − 2I₃)/4 + (9 − 2I₃)/3 = I₃. 12 se multiply: 42 − 6I₃ + 36 − 8I₃ = 12I₃ ⇒ 78 = 26I₃ ⇒ I₃ = 3 A. Phir I₁ = 2 A, I₂ = 1 A, aur check 2 + 1 = 3 ✓. 2 A aur 1 A to I₁ aur I₂ hain — galat unknown report karne ka trap; 5.2 A tab aata hai jab right side ke I₃ ko 12 se multiply karna bhool jao (78 = 15I₃).

weeks.title: Sequences and their limits
weeks.summary: Is week aap sequences ko bounded, monotonic, convergent aur divergent ke hisaab se pehchanna seekhoge, limit ki exact definition samjhoge, aur monotone convergence theorem se recursive sequences ki limit nikaloge.
concepts: **Sequence**: natural numbers se real numbers ka function, a₁, a₂, a₃, ... Formula se (aₙ = 1/n) ya recursion se (aₙ₊₁ = √(2 + aₙ)) diya ja sakta hai. Jaise ek ADC har 1 ms par capacitor voltage sample kare — samples ki list ek sequence hai.
**Bounded**: koi M ho jisse |aₙ| ≤ M har n ke liye. Sirf upar se rukna = bounded above, sirf neeche se = bounded below. aₙ = (−1)ⁿ bounded hai, aₙ = n nahi.
**Monotonic**: har n ke liye aₙ₊₁ ≥ aₙ (increasing) ya aₙ₊₁ ≤ aₙ (decreasing). Check karne ke liye aₙ₊₁ − aₙ ka sign dekho, ya positive terms me aₙ₊₁/aₙ ko 1 se compare karo.

**Limit (convergence)**: aₙ → L ka matlab: koi bhi chhota ε > 0 do, ek N mil jaata hai jiske baad har term |aₙ − L| < ε me rehti hai. Matlab tail poori ki poori L ke paas aa jaati hai, sirf kuch terms nahi.

**Divergent**: jo converge na kare. Do tarah: ∞ ki taraf bhaagna (aₙ = n²) ya oscillate karna ((−1)ⁿ, jo 1 aur −1 ke beech koodta rehta hai). Convergent ⇒ bounded, par bounded ⇒ convergent zaroori nahi.

**Limit rules aur standard limits**: sum, product, quotient (denominator ki limit ≠ 0) ki limit = limits ka sum/product/quotient. Yaad rakho: 1/nᵖ → 0 (p > 0), rⁿ → 0 agar |r| < 1, n^(1/n) → 1, (1 + x/n)ⁿ → eˣ. Rational expressions me sabse badi power se divide karo.
**Sandwich theorem**: bₙ ≤ aₙ ≤ cₙ aur bₙ, cₙ dono L par jaayein to aₙ → L. Example: −1/n ≤ (sin n)/n ≤ 1/n ⇒ (sin n)/n → 0.

**Monotone convergence theorem**: monotonic + bounded sequence hamesha converge karta hai. Increasing aur bounded above ⇒ apne supremum par converge. Recursive sequences ke liye pehle ye dikhao, phir limit L ko recursion me rakh ke solve karo.

example.problem: a₁ = 1 aur aₙ₊₁ = √(2 + aₙ). Dikhao ki ye sequence converge karta hai aur limit nikalo.
steps: Kuch terms: a₁ = 1, a₂ = √3 ≈ 1.732, a₃ = √3.732 ≈ 1.932 — badh rahe hain.
Bounded: agar aₙ < 2 to aₙ₊₁ = √(2 + aₙ) < √4 = 2. a₁ = 1 < 2 se induction se har aₙ < 2.
Increasing: aₙ₊₁² − aₙ² = 2 + aₙ − aₙ² = (2 − aₙ)(1 + aₙ) > 0, kyunki 0 < aₙ < 2. To aₙ₊₁ > aₙ.
Monotone convergence theorem se limit L exist karti hai.
Recursion me limit lo: L = √(2 + L) ⇒ L² − L − 2 = 0 ⇒ (L − 2)(L + 1) = 0.
Saare terms positive hain, to L = −1 reject.
Answer: sequence converge karta hai aur **limit L = 2**.

mistakes: Pehle convergence prove kiye bina L = f(L) solve kar dena. Jaise aₙ₊₁ = 2aₙ ke liye L = 2L ⇒ L = 0 aata hai, jabki a₁ = 1 se sequence 1, 2, 4, ... diverge karta hai.
Bounded hone ko convergence samajhna. (−1)ⁿ bounded hai par converge nahi karta; monotonic bhi hona chahiye.
|aₙ − L| < ε me strict < ko ≤ samajh kar N ek kam le lena. Boundary wale term ko alag se check karo.
revision: Rational sequence: highest power se divide karo; same degree ⇒ leading coefficients ka ratio.
Recursive limit: pehle convergence, phir L = f(L), phir galat root hatao.

questions.question: lim (n → ∞) (3n² + 2n)/(5n² − 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Upar-neeche n² se divide karo: (3 + 2/n)/(5 − 1/n²) → 3/5. Numerator aur denominator ki degree same hai, to limit leading coefficients ka ratio hai. 2/5 tab aata hai jab n wale term ko leading samajh lo.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa sequence bounded hai par convergent NAHI?
questions.explanation: (−1)ⁿ = −1, 1, −1, 1, ... hamesha [−1, 1] me rehta hai (bounded), par kisi ek number ke paas settle nahi hota, to divergent. 1/n aur 1 + 1/n² bounded bhi hain aur converge bhi karte hain (0 aur 1 par). aₙ = n unbounded hai.

questions.question: aₙ = n/(n + 1) ke baare me kaunsa statement sahi hai?
questions.explanation: aₙ₊₁ − aₙ = (n + 1)/(n + 2) − n/(n + 1) = 1/((n + 1)(n + 2)) > 0, to increasing. aₙ = 1 − 1/(n + 1) < 1, to bounded above, aur limit 1. Terms 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, ... hain — 'decreasing, limit 1' wala trap tab lagta hai jab sirf limit yaad ho, direction nahi.

questions.question: aₙ = 2/n ke liye sabse chhota natural number N kya hai jisse har n ≥ N par |aₙ − 0| < 0.01 ho?
questions.explanation: 2/n < 0.01 ⇔ n > 200. n = 200 par 2/200 = 0.01 exactly, jo strictly 0.01 se chhota nahi. Isliye pehla valid n = 201, aur uske baad sab chhote hain. 200 strict inequality ko ≤ padhne ka trap hai; 100 tab aata hai jab 2 ka factor bhool jao.

questions.question: lim (n → ∞) (1 + 2/n)ⁿ kya hai?
questions.explanation: Standard result (1 + x/n)ⁿ → eˣ, yahan x = 2, to limit e² hai. '1' wala trap ye sochne se aata hai ki 1 + 2/n → 1 aur 1 ki koi bhi power 1 — par power n bhi saath me ∞ ja rahi hai, isliye ye 1^∞ form indeterminate hai.

questions.question: a₁ = 1 aur aₙ₊₁ = √(6 + aₙ). Ye sequence increasing aur bounded hai. Iski limit kya hai?
questions.explanation: Monotone convergence theorem se limit L exist karti hai. L = √(6 + L) ⇒ L² − L − 6 = 0 ⇒ (L − 3)(L + 2) = 0. Saare terms positive hain, to L = −2 reject, L = 3. √7 sirf a₂ hai — doosre term ko limit samajhne ka trap; −2 galat root hai.

questions.question: aₙ = (−1)ⁿ/n ki limit kya hai?
options: Exist nahi karti, kyunki sign badalta rehta hai
questions.explanation: −1/n ≤ (−1)ⁿ/n ≤ 1/n, aur dono taraf 1/n → 0, to sandwich theorem se aₙ → 0. Sign badalna limit ko nahi rokta jab terms ka size khud 0 par ja raha ho — ise (−1)ⁿ (jo ±1 par atka rehta hai) se confuse karna yahan ka trap hai. −1 aur 1 sirf pehle terms ka sign ya size dekh ke lagaye guess hain.

questions.question: a₁ = 2 aur aₙ₊₁ = 3aₙ − 1. a₄ kya hai?
questions.explanation: a₂ = 3·2 − 1 = 5, a₃ = 3·5 − 1 = 14, a₄ = 3·14 − 1 = 41. 14 sirf a₃ hai — ek step kam ginne ka trap; 122 ek step zyada (a₅) hai; 42 tab aata hai jab aakhri step me −1 bhool jao.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa sequence decreasing hai?
questions.explanation: aₙ₊₁ − aₙ = 1/(n + 1) − 1/n = −1/(n(n + 1)) < 0, to 1 + 1/n har step par ghatta hai (2, 1.5, 1.33, ...). n² aur 2ⁿ increasing hain. (−1)ⁿ/n monotonic hi nahi — sign ki wajah se upar-neeche koodta hai (−1, 0.5, −0.33, ...), bhale hi uska size ghat raha ho; size ghatne ko decreasing samajhna trap hai.

questions.question: lim (n → ∞) [√(n² + 4n) − n] kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∞ − ∞ form hai, to conjugate se multiply karo: [√(n² + 4n) − n]·[√(n² + 4n) + n]/[√(n² + 4n) + n] = 4n/[√(n² + 4n) + n]. Upar-neeche n se divide: 4/[√(1 + 4/n) + 1] → 4/2 = 2. 0 '∞ − ∞ = 0' maan lene ka trap hai; 4 tab aata hai jab neeche ke do terms (√ wala aur n) ko ek hi gin lo.

questions.question: lim (n → ∞) (1 − 3/n)^(2n) kya hai?
questions.explanation: (1 − 3/n)^(2n) = [(1 − 3/n)ⁿ]². Standard limit (1 + x/n)ⁿ → eˣ me x = −3, to andar wala e^(−3) par jaata hai aur poora (e^(−3))² = e^(−6). e^(−3) power ka 2 bhoolne ka trap hai; e⁶ minus sign chhodne ka; 1 '1^∞ = 1' wala galat shortcut hai.

questions.question: lim (n → ∞) (2ⁿ + 5ⁿ)^(1/n) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Bada term 5ⁿ hai. 5ⁿ ≤ 2ⁿ + 5ⁿ ≤ 2·5ⁿ, to 1/n power lo: 5 ≤ aₙ ≤ 2^(1/n)·5. 2^(1/n) → 1, isliye sandwich se limit 5. 7 = 2 + 5 bases ko jod dene ka trap hai; 2 chhota base hai jo jaldi negligible ho jaata hai; ∞ tab lagta hai jab sirf andar ka badhna dekho aur 1/n power ko ignore karo.

questions.question: aₙ = (3n + 1)/(n + 2) ki limit 3 hai. Sabse chhota natural number N kya hai jisse har n ≥ N par |aₙ − 3| < 0.05 ho?
questions.explanation: |aₙ − 3| = |3n + 1 − 3n − 6|/(n + 2) = 5/(n + 2). 5/(n + 2) < 0.05 ⇔ n + 2 > 100 ⇔ n > 98. n = 98 par 5/100 = 0.05 exactly, jo strictly chhota nahi, to N = 99. 98 strict < ko ≤ padhne ka trap hai; 101 tab aata hai jab neeche ka +2 chhod ke 5/n < 0.05 solve karo; 100 n + 2 = 100 ko hi N maan lena hai.

questions.question: a₁ = 2 aur aₙ₊₁ = 4 − 3/aₙ. Ye sequence converge karta hai. Iski limit kya hai?
questions.explanation: Limit L ho to L = 4 − 3/L ⇒ L² − 4L + 3 = 0 ⇒ L = 1 ya 3. Ab sequence dekho: a₂ = 2.5, a₃ = 2.8, a₄ ≈ 2.93 — increasing. Aur agar aₙ < 3 to 3/aₙ > 1, isliye aₙ₊₁ < 3: sequence 3 se upar nahi jaata. Increasing hai aur 2 se shuru, to 1 par kabhi nahi aa sakta; monotone + bounded ⇒ limit 3. '1 ya 3' quadratic ke dono roots bina check kiye le lena hai — sahi root starting value aur monotonicity se chunna padta hai.

questions.question: lim (n → ∞) (3ⁿ + n³)/(3ⁿ⁺¹ + 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Upar-neeche 3ⁿ se divide karo: (1 + n³/3ⁿ)/(3 + 2/3ⁿ). Exponential har power se tez badhta hai, isliye n³/3ⁿ → 0, aur 2/3ⁿ → 0. Limit = 1/3. 1 tab aata hai jab 3ⁿ⁺¹ ko 3ⁿ jaisa hi maan lo — wo 3 guna hai, yahi trap; 3 ratio ulta lena hai; 0 tab aata hai jab n³ ko upar ka dominant term maan ke kuch aur galat cancel kar do.

weeks.title: Limits of functions and continuity
weeks.summary: Is week aap function ki limit nikalna seekhoge — factoring, rationalising, one-sided limits, ∞ par limits, aur exponential vs power ki race — aur phir continuity ki teen-step definition se piecewise functions check karoge.
concepts: **Limit ka idea**: lim (x → a) f(x) = L ka matlab x ko a ke jitna chaho paas le jao (par a ke barabar nahi), f(x) L ke utna paas aa jaata hai. f(a) ki value kya hai ya defined hai bhi ya nahi — limit ko isse farak nahi padta.

**One-sided limits**: x → a⁻ (left se) aur x → a⁺ (right se). Two-sided limit tabhi exist karti hai jab dono barabar hon. Unit step u(t) ke liye t → 0⁻ par 0 aur t → 0⁺ par 1, isliye t = 0 par limit nahi hai.

**0/0 forms todna**: direct substitution se 0/0 aaye to factor karke cancel karo ((x² − 9)/(x − 3) = x + 3), ya √ wale expressions me conjugate se multiply karo (rationalise). Ek standard result: lim (x → 0) sin x / x = 1 (x radian me).

**Limits at infinity**: rational function me sabse badi power se divide karo. Degree upar = neeche ⇒ leading coefficients ka ratio; upar chhoti ⇒ 0; upar badi ⇒ ±∞. Finite limit L ho to y = L **horizontal asymptote** hai.

**Powers vs exponentials**: x → ∞ par eˣ har power xⁿ se tez badhta hai, aur ln x har positive power se dheere. Isliye xⁿe^(−x) → 0 aur (ln x)/x → 0. RC discharge v(t) = V₀e^(−t/RC) bhi t → ∞ par 0 jaata hai, chahe aage koi polynomial factor ho.

**Continuity at a**: teen cheezein chahiye — (1) f(a) defined, (2) lim (x → a) f(x) exist kare, (3) dono barabar hon. Polynomials, eˣ, sin, cos har jagah continuous hain; rational functions apne domain me.

**Discontinuity ke types**: removable (limit hai par f(a) alag ya undefined — hole), jump (left aur right limit alag, jaise u(t)), infinite (1/x jaisa vertical asymptote). **Intermediate value theorem**: [a, b] par continuous f, f(a) aur f(b) ke beech ki har value kahin na kahin leta hai.

example.problem: f(x) = kx + 1 jab x < 2, aur f(x) = x² − 1 jab x ≥ 2. k ki kis value par f, x = 2 par continuous hoga?
steps: Continuity ke liye left limit = right limit = f(2): 2k + 1 = 3.
Answer: **k = 1** par f(x) = x + 1 (left) aur x² − 1 (right) x = 2 par jud jaate hain, dono 3 dete hain.

mistakes: 0/0 aate hi 'limit exist nahi karti' likh dena. 0/0 indeterminate hai — iska matlab hai aur kaam karo (factor ya rationalise), answer nahi.
sin(5x)/(2x) me x → 0 par sirf 1 likh dena. sin(ax)/(bx) = (a/b)·sin(ax)/(ax) → a/b; andar aur neeche ka argument match karwao.
Piecewise function me sirf ek side check karna. Joint par left limit, right limit aur f(a) — teeno barabar hone chahiye.
revision: Limit exists ⇔ left limit = right limit.
x → ∞: same degree ⇒ leading coefficients ka ratio.
eˣ har power se tez; xⁿe^(−x) → 0.
Continuous at a ⇔ lim (x → a) f(x) = f(a).

questions.question: lim (x → 3) (x² − 9)/(x − 3) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Direct rakhne par 0/0. Factor karo: (x − 3)(x + 3)/(x − 3) = x + 3 (x ≠ 3 ke liye), aur x → 3 par 6. 0/0 dekh kar 'exist nahi karti' bolna trap hai — 0/0 sirf indeterminate form hai.

questions.question: lim (x → ∞) (4x³ − x)/(2x³ + 5x²) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Upar-neeche x³ se divide: (4 − 1/x²)/(2 + 5/x) → 4/2 = 2. Degrees same hain, to leading coefficients ka ratio. 4/5 tab aata hai jab neeche 5x² ko leading term maan lo.

questions.question: f(x) = |x|/x (x ≠ 0) ke liye x → 0 par kya sahi hai?
options: Left limit −1, right limit 1, isliye limit exist nahi karti
Left aur right dono 1 hain, limit 1 hai
f(0) defined nahi, isliye left aur right limit bhi nahi hain
questions.explanation: x > 0 par |x|/x = 1, x < 0 par |x|/x = −1. To right limit 1 aur left limit −1 — alag hain, isliye two-sided limit exist nahi karti (jump). Last option ka trap: f(0) undefined hone se one-sided limits par koi asar nahi padta.

questions.question: lim (x → 0) sin(5x)/(2x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: sin(5x)/(2x) = (5/2)·sin(5x)/(5x). Jaise x → 0, 5x → 0 aur sin(5x)/(5x) → 1, to answer 5/2. '1' wala trap tab hota hai jab sin u / u = 1 seedha laga do bina argument match kiye; 2/5 me ratio ulta ho gaya.

questions.question: lim (x → ∞) x³e^(−x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: x³e^(−x) = x³/eˣ, aur eˣ har power se tez badhta hai, to ratio 0 ki taraf jaata hai. (L'Hôpital teen baar lagao to 6/eˣ → 0 milta hai.) ∞ wala trap ye sochne se aata hai ki x³ bhi to ∞ ja raha hai — par race exponential jeetta hai.

questions.question: f(x) = ax + b (x < 1), f(1) = 3, aur f(x) = x² + a (x > 1). Agar f har jagah continuous hai, to a aur b kya hain?
questions.explanation: Right limit: 1 + a = 3 ⇒ a = 2. Left limit: a + b = 3 ⇒ b = 1. To a = 2, b = 1 (left me 2x + 1, right me x² + 2, dono x = 1 par 3). 'a = 2, b = 3' tab aata hai jab b ko hi f(1) samajh lo; 'a = 1, b = 2' sirf left side wali condition (a + b = 3) satisfy karta hai — right side par 1 + 1 = 2 ≠ 3.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x + 1 (x < 1) aur f(x) = 5 (x ≥ 1). x → 1 par limit ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: Left limit 3, right limit 5, isliye limit exist nahi karti
questions.explanation: Left se: 2(1) + 1 = 3. Right se: 5. Dono alag, to two-sided limit exist nahi karti — ye jump hai. f(1) = 5 hone se limit 5 nahi ho jaati; limit f(a) ki value par depend nahi karti. Sirf ek side dekh ke 3 bolna aur 3, 5 ka average 4 lena dono traps hain.

questions.question: lim (x → ∞) (3x² + 1)/(x³ − 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Upar degree 2, neeche degree 3. x³ se divide karo: (3/x + 1/x³)/(1 − 2/x³) → 0/1 = 0. Upar ki degree chhoti ⇒ 0. 3 leading coefficients ka ratio hai jo sirf barabar degree par lagta hai — yahi trap; ∞ degrees ka comparison ulta karne se aata hai.

questions.question: f(x) = (x² − 1)/(x − 1) (x ≠ 1) aur f(1) = 5. x = 1 par f kaisa hai?
questions.explanation: x ≠ 1 par f(x) = x + 1, to lim (x → 1) f(x) = 2 dono side se exist karti hai. Par f(1) = 5 ≠ 2, to continuity fail — limit hai, sirf value galat hai, yaani removable (f(1) = 2 kar do to theek). Jump tab hota jab left aur right limit alag hote; infinite tab jab function blow up karta; 'continuous' tab jab f(1) bhi 2 hota.

questions.question: lim (x → 0) [√(x + 9) − 3]/x kya hai?
questions.explanation: Direct rakhne par 0/0. Conjugate se multiply: [(x + 9) − 9]/[x(√(x + 9) + 3)] = 1/(√(x + 9) + 3) → 1/(3 + 3) = 1/6. 1/3 tab aata hai jab neeche sirf ek 3 lo; 6 reciprocal ulta karne ka; 0 '0/0 = 0' maan lene ka trap hai.

questions.question: lim (x → 0) sin(3x)/sin(7x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Likho: [sin(3x)/(3x)]·[(7x)/sin(7x)]·(3x/7x). Pehle do factors 1 par jaate hain, aur 3x/7x = 3/7. To limit 3/7. 1 'sin ko sin se cancel' kar dene ka trap hai; 7/3 ratio ulta lena hai; 0/0 dekh ke 0 likhna bhi galat hai.

questions.question: f(x) = x³ − 4x + 1. Integers par values check karke batao, intermediate value theorem [−3, 2] me kitne real roots ki guarantee deta hai?
questions.explanation: f(−3) = −14, f(−2) = 1, f(−1) = 4, f(0) = 1, f(1) = −2, f(2) = 1. Sign (−3, −2), (0, 1) aur (1, 2) me badalta hai — teen alag intervals, to IVT se teen roots. Cubic ke 3 se zyada roots nahi ho sakte, to exactly 3. 1 tab aata hai jab pehla sign change dekh ke ruk jao; 2 tab jab f(1) calculate na karo aur (0, 2) ko ek hi interval maan lo — wahan do baar sign badalta hai.

questions.question: lim (x → −∞) (2x + 1)/√(x² + 3) kya hai?
questions.explanation: √(x² + 3) = |x|·√(1 + 3/x²), aur x < 0 par |x| = −x. To expression = (2x + 1)/(−x·√(1 + 3/x²)) = (2 + 1/x)/(−√(1 + 3/x²)) → 2/(−1) = −2. 2 tab aata hai jab √(x²) = x le lo — negative x ke liye ye galat hai, yahi trap. Upar aur neeche dono degree 1 ki tarah badhte hain, isliye 0 nahi, aur limit finite hai.

questions.question: lim (x → 2) (x² + ax + b)/(x − 2) = 7 ho, to a aur b kya hain?
questions.explanation: Neeche x − 2 → 0 hai, to finite limit ke liye upar bhi 0 hona chahiye: 4 + 2a + b = 0. Tab upar = (x − 2)(x + m) jahan m = a + 2, aur limit = 2 + m = 7 ⇒ m = 5 ⇒ a = 3, b = −10. Check: x² + 3x − 10 = (x − 2)(x + 5) → 7 ✓. Baaki teeno options bhi 4 + 2a + b = 0 satisfy karte hain — sirf pehli condition lagana trap hai. a = 5, b = −14 tab aata hai jab m ko hi 7 maan lo (limit 9 deta hai); a = −3, b = 2 limit 1 deta hai.

questions.question: f(x) = (3eˣ + 2)/(eˣ − 1) ke horizontal asymptotes kya hain?
questions.explanation: x → ∞: upar-neeche eˣ se divide karo: (3 + 2e^(−x))/(1 − e^(−x)) → 3. x → −∞: eˣ → 0, to f → (0 + 2)/(0 − 1) = −2. Do alag asymptotes: y = 3 aur y = −2. 'Sirf y = 3' sirf ek direction check karne ka trap hai; y = 2 neeche ke −1 ka sign bhool jaane se aata hai.

weeks.title: Derivatives and the rules of differentiation
weeks.summary: Is week aap derivative ko limit se define karoge, use slope aur rate of change ki tarah samjhoge, aur power, product, quotient aur chain rule se polynomials, rational functions aur higher-order derivatives nikaloge.
concepts: **Derivative ki definition**: f'(a) = lim (h → 0) [f(a + h) − f(a)]/h. Ye graph par x = a wali tangent line ki slope hai, aur physically 'instantaneous rate of change'. Circuits me i = C·dv/dt (capacitor) aur v = L·di/dt (inductor) isi idea par chalte hain.

**Differentiable ⇒ continuous**, par ulta zaroori nahi. |x| x = 0 par continuous hai, lekin left slope −1 aur right slope +1 alag hain, isliye wahan derivative nahi hai (corner). Jump wale point par to derivative ka sawaal hi nahi.
**Basic rules**: (c)' = 0, (xⁿ)' = nxⁿ⁻¹ (har real n ke liye, jaise (√x)' = 1/(2√x)), (cf)' = cf', (f ± g)' = f' ± g'. Isse koi bhi polynomial term-by-term differentiate hota hai.

**Product rule**: (uv)' = u'v + uv'. **Quotient rule**: (u/v)' = (u'v − uv')/v², v ≠ 0. Quotient rule me numerator ka order yaad rakho: 'neeche wala × upar ka derivative − upar wala × neeche ka derivative'.
**Chain rule**: (f(g(x)))' = f'(g(x))·g'(x) — bahar wale ka derivative (andar wala as it is) × andar wale ka derivative. Jaise ((2x + 1)⁵)' = 5(2x + 1)⁴·2.
**Higher-order derivatives**: f'' = (f')' curvature/acceleration batata hai, f''' aage. Polynomial of degree n ka (n + 1)th derivative 0 hota hai. Position s(t) ⇒ velocity s' ⇒ acceleration s''.
**Tangent line**: x = a par y = f(a) + f'(a)(x − a). Ye f ka sabse achha local straight-line approximation hai — aage week me linearisation aur error estimate isi se aayenge.

example.problem: f(x) = (x² + 1)/(x − 1) ka derivative nikalo aur f'(2) batao.
steps: u = x² + 1, v = x − 1, to u' = 2x aur v' = 1.
Answer: **f'(2) = −1**, yaani x = 2 par graph −1 slope se neeche ja raha hai.

mistakes: Quotient rule me numerator ulta likhna (uv' − u'v). Isse answer ka sign hi badal jaata hai; 'low d-high minus high d-low' yaad rakho.
Chain rule me andar wale ka derivative bhool jaana: ((3x + 2)⁴)' = 4(3x + 2)³·3, sirf 4(3x + 2)³ nahi.
Product ka derivative ko derivatives ka product samajhna: (uv)' ≠ u'·v'.
revision: Tangent at a: y = f(a) + f'(a)(x − a).

questions.question: d/dx (4x³ − 5x + 7) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Term-by-term: (4x³)' = 12x², (−5x)' = −5, (7)' = 0. Total 12x² − 5. Constant ka derivative 0 hai, isliye '+ 7' wala option galat hai; 12x² − 5x me −5x ka derivative likhna hi bhool gaye.

questions.question: lim (h → 0) [(3 + h)² − 9]/h ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: (3 + h)² − 9 = 6h + h², to expression = 6 + h → 6. Ye f(x) = x² ka x = 3 par derivative hai: f'(3) = 2·3 = 6. 9 wala trap f(3) hai, derivative nahi; 0 tab aata hai jab h = 0 seedha rakh ke 0/0 ko 0 maan lo.

questions.question: 10 μF capacitor ke across voltage v(t) = 4t³ volt hai (t second me). t = 1 s par current i = C·dv/dt kitna hai?
questions.explanation: dv/dt = 12t², t = 1 par 12 V/s. i = 10 μF × 12 V/s = 120 μA. 40 μA = C·v(1) hai — derivative lena bhool gaye. 240 μA second derivative (24t) se aata hai, aur 12 μA me C ka 10 guna factor chhoot gaya.

questions.question: f(x) = x/(x² + 1) ho to f'(2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Quotient rule: f'(x) = [1·(x² + 1) − x·2x]/(x² + 1)² = (1 − x²)/(x² + 1)². x = 2: (1 − 4)/25 = −3/25. 3/25 numerator ka order ulta likhne se aata hai; −3/5 me denominator ka square bhool gaye; 1/4 = 1/(2x) to sirf 'upar ka derivative ÷ neeche ka derivative' hai, jo galat rule hai.

questions.question: Curve y = x³ − 2x par x = 1 wale point par tangent line kaunsi hai?
questions.explanation: y(1) = 1 − 2 = −1, to point (1, −1). y' = 3x² − 2, to slope y'(1) = 1. Tangent: y + 1 = 1·(x − 1) ⇒ y = x − 2. y = 3x − 4 me −2x ke derivative wala −2 chhoot gaya (slope 3 le liya); y = x − 1 slope sahi hai par point (1, 0) le liya.

questions.question: f(x) = (x² + 1)³ ho to f''(1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Chain rule: f'(x) = 3(x² + 1)²·2x = 6x(x² + 1)². Product rule se f''(x) = 6(x² + 1)² + 6x·2(x² + 1)·2x = 6(x² + 1)² + 24x²(x² + 1). x = 1: 6·4 + 24·2 = 24 + 48 = 72. 24 sirf pehla term hai (ya f'(1)) — product rule ka doosra hissa bhool gaye; 48 sirf doosra term hai.

questions.question: d/dx (√x + 1/x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: √x = x^(1/2) ⇒ (1/2)x^(−1/2) = 1/(2√x). 1/x = x^(−1) ⇒ −x^(−2) = −1/x². Sum: 1/(2√x) − 1/x². + 1/x² wala option power rule ke −1 ka sign chhodta hai; 1/√x me 1/2 factor gaayab hai; 2√x power ko neeche laane ki jagah ulta upar le jaane ka trap hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa function x = 0 par continuous hai par differentiable NAHI?
questions.explanation: |x| ka graph x = 0 par corner banata hai: left slope −1, right slope +1, isliye derivative nahi, jabki function continuous hai. x² aur x³ + x polynomials hain — har jagah differentiable. u(x) x = 0 par jump karta hai, to continuous hi nahi — 'differentiable nahi' sahi hai par continuity wali shart fail hoti hai.

questions.question: d/dx (3x − 1)⁴ kya hai?
questions.explanation: Chain rule: bahar wale ka derivative 4(3x − 1)³, andar wale (3x − 1) ka derivative 3. Product: 12(3x − 1)³. 4(3x − 1)³ andar ka factor 3 bhoolne ka classic trap hai; 12(3x − 1)⁴ me power ghatana bhool gaye; 3(3x − 1)³ me bahar ka 4 chhoot gaya.

questions.question: f(x) = (x² + 1)(2x − 3) ho to f'(1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Product rule: f' = (2x)(2x − 3) + (x² + 1)(2). x = 1: 2·(−1) + 2·2 = −2 + 4 = 2. 4 = u'·v' = 2·2, jo '(uv)' = u'·v'' wala trap hai; −2 sirf pehla term hai, doosra bhool gaye.

questions.question: Ek particle ki position s(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t hai. Velocity kin t par zero hoti hai, aur t = 3 par acceleration kya hai?
questions.explanation: v = s' = 3t² − 12t + 9 = 3(t − 1)(t − 3), to v = 0 at t = 1 aur t = 3. a = s'' = 6t − 12, to a(3) = 18 − 12 = 6. 'a = 0' velocity zero ko acceleration zero samajhne ka trap hai — rukne ke pal bhi acceleration ho sakta hai; t = 2 par a = 0 hai, v nahi; t = 0, 3 to s(t) = 0 wale roots hain.

questions.question: 0.2 H inductor me current i(t) = 2t²/(t + 1) ampere hai (t second me). t = 1 s par voltage v = L·di/dt kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Quotient rule: di/dt = [4t(t + 1) − 2t²·1]/(t + 1)² = (2t² + 4t)/(t + 1)². t = 1: 6/4 = 1.5 A/s. v = 0.2 × 1.5 = 0.3 V. −0.3 V numerator ulta likhne (uv' − u'v) ka trap hai; 0.6 V tab aata hai jab neeche ka square bhool jao (6/2); 0.2 V current i(1) = 1 A ko hi derivative maan lena hai.

questions.question: Origin se curve y = x² + 4 par tangent lines kheenchi jaati hain. Inki slopes kya hain?
questions.explanation: x = a par tangent: y = (a² + 4) + 2a(x − a). Origin is par ho: 0 = a² + 4 − 2a² ⇒ a² = 4 ⇒ a = ±2. Slope = 2a = ±4. ±2 touching points ke x-coordinates hain, slopes nahi — yahi trap; 0 vertex (x = 0) ki slope hai, par wahan ki tangent y = 4 origin se nahi guzarti; ±8 slope ko 2a ki jagah a³ jaisa galat lene se aata hai.

questions.question: f(x) = x² (x ≤ 1) aur f(x) = ax + b (x > 1). Agar f x = 1 par differentiable hai, to a aur b kya hain?
questions.explanation: Differentiable ⇒ pehle continuous: 1² = a + b. Phir dono side ki slopes barabar: left slope 2x = 2, right slope a ⇒ a = 2. To b = 1 − 2 = −1. a = 1, b = 0 sirf continuity se ek guess hai — slope wali condition chhoot gayi; a = 2, b = 1 me continuity ka equation galat (a − b = 1) solve hua; a = −1, b = 2 bhi sirf continuity satisfy karta hai. Dono conditions chahiye.

questions.question: f(x) = x/(x + 1) ho to f''(1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: f' = [(x + 1) − x]/(x + 1)² = 1/(x + 1)² = (x + 1)^(−2). f'' = −2(x + 1)^(−3) = −2/(x + 1)³. x = 1: −2/8 = −1/4. 1/4 sirf f'(1) hai — ek derivative kam lene ka trap; −1/2 tab aata hai jab power −3 ki jagah −2 hi rakh do (−2/4); 1/8 me −2 ka factor aur sign dono chhoot gaye.

weeks.title: Mean value theorem, L'Hôpital and Taylor polynomials
weeks.summary: Is week aap derivative ke bade theorems use karoge: MVT aur monotonicity, L'Hôpital se 0/0 limits, inverse function ka derivative, differentials se measurement error ka estimate, aur Taylor polynomial se functions ka approximation.
concepts: **Rolle's theorem**: f [a, b] par continuous, (a, b) me differentiable, aur f(a) = f(b) ⇒ koi c ∈ (a, b) jahan f'(c) = 0. Seedhi baat: jo function wapas usi height par aaye, beech me kahin flat hua hoga.

**Mean value theorem (MVT)**: same conditions (bina f(a) = f(b) ke) ⇒ koi c ∈ (a, b) jahan f'(c) = [f(b) − f(a)]/(b − a). Kisi pal par instantaneous rate = average rate. Jaise 2 ghante me 120 km chale to kisi pal speedometer ne exactly 60 km/h dikhaya.

**Monotonicity**: interval par f' > 0 ⇒ f increasing, f' < 0 ⇒ decreasing (ye MVT se hi prove hota hai). Critical points (f' = 0) ke aas-paas f' ka sign badle to local max ya min: + se − ⇒ max, − se + ⇒ min.

**L'Hôpital's rule**: lim f/g me 0/0 ya ∞/∞ form ho to lim f/g = lim f'/g' (agar ye limit exist kare). Har baar dobara check karo ki form abhi bhi 0/0 ya ∞/∞ hai; nahi hai to rule mat lagao. Quotient rule NAHI lagta — upar aur neeche alag-alag differentiate karo.
**Inverse function ka derivative**: y = f(x) aur f'(x) ≠ 0 ho to (f⁻¹)'(y) = 1/f'(x). Dhyan: y par evaluate karne ke liye pehle wo x dhoondo jiske liye f(x) = y.
**Differentials aur errors**: dy = f'(x)·dx, yaani Δy ≈ f'(x)Δx. Relative error ke liye y = kxⁿ me Δy/y ≈ n·Δx/x. Jaise P = V²/R me V ka 1% error P me lagbhag 2% error deta hai.

**Taylor polynomial**: a ke paas f(x) ≈ Pₙ(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x − a) + f''(a)(x − a)²/2! + ... + f⁽ⁿ⁾(a)(x − a)ⁿ/n!. **Taylor's theorem**: error Rₙ = f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(c)(x − a)ⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1)! kisi c ke liye. Standard: eˣ ≈ 1 + x + x²/2, sin x ≈ x − x³/6, cos x ≈ 1 − x²/2, ln(1 + x) ≈ x − x²/2.

example.problem: Differential (linear approximation) se √4.1 ka andaza lagao aur error dekho.
steps: f(x) = √x lo aur a = 4 chuno, kyunki √4 = 2 exactly pata hai.
Asli value √4.1 ≈ 2.02485, to error lagbhag 0.00015 hai.
Taylor ka agla term f''(4)(0.1)²/2 = (−1/32)(0.01)/2 ≈ −0.00016 lagbhag yahi gap bharta hai.
Answer: **√4.1 ≈ 2.025** (degree-1 Taylor polynomial), jo 4 decimal tak almost sahi hai.

mistakes: L'Hôpital me quotient rule laga dena. Rule hai f'/g', na ki (f/g)'. Aur 0/0 ya ∞/∞ check kiye bina lagana galat answer deta hai.
(f⁻¹)'(y) nikalte waqt f' ko y par evaluate kar dena. Pehle f(x) = y solve karke x lo, phir 1/f'(x).
Relative error me power ka factor bhool jaana: y = x³ me 1% error x me ⇒ lagbhag 3% error y me, 1% nahi.
revision: L'Hôpital: 0/0 ya ∞/∞ ⇒ lim f/g = lim f'/g'.
eˣ ≈ 1 + x + x²/2; ln(1 + x) ≈ x − x²/2.

questions.question: f(x) = x² ke liye interval [1, 3] par mean value theorem jis c ki guarantee deta hai, wo kya hai?
questions.explanation: Average slope = (9 − 1)/(3 − 1) = 4. f'(c) = 2c = 4 ⇒ c = 2, jo (1, 3) ke andar hai. 1 aur 3 endpoints hain — MVT ka c hamesha open interval ke andar hota hai.

questions.question: f(x) = x³ − 12x kis interval par decreasing hai?
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 3x² − 12 = 3(x − 2)(x + 2). Ye −2 < x < 2 par negative hai, to f wahan decreasing hai. (2, ∞) aur (−∞, −2) par f' > 0, to wahan increasing — sign chart ulta padhne ka trap.

questions.question: lim (x → 0) (eˣ − 1 − x)/x² kya hai?
questions.explanation: 0/0 form ⇒ L'Hôpital: (eˣ − 1)/(2x), abhi bhi 0/0 ⇒ phir se: eˣ/2 → 1/2. Taylor se bhi: eˣ − 1 − x ≈ x²/2. '1' wala trap tab aata hai jab doosri baar neeche ke 2x ka derivative 2 lena bhool jao.

questions.question: Resistor me power P = V²/R. Agar V ke measurement me 2% error hai (R exact hai), to P me lagbhag kitna relative error aayega?
questions.explanation: dP = (2V/R)dV, to dP/P = 2·dV/V = 2 × 2% = 4%. Power 2 hai, isliye error double hota hai. 2% wala trap ye maanna hai ki error jaisa ka taisa aage jaata hai; 1% me power se multiply ki jagah divide kar diya.

questions.question: f(x) = x³ + x + 1 one-one hai. (f⁻¹)'(3) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Pehle wo x dhoondo jiske liye f(x) = 3: x³ + x + 1 = 3 ⇒ x = 1. f'(x) = 3x² + 1, to f'(1) = 4. (f⁻¹)'(3) = 1/f'(1) = 1/4. 1/28 tab aata hai jab f' ko seedha 3 par evaluate kar do (f'(3) = 28) — sabse common trap.

questions.question: ln(1 + x) ka 0 ke paas degree-2 Taylor polynomial use karke ln(1.1) ka approximate value kya milta hai?
questions.explanation: f = ln(1 + x): f(0) = 0, f'(0) = 1, f''(0) = −1, to P₂(x) = x − x²/2. x = 0.1: 0.1 − 0.01/2 = 0.095 (asli value ≈ 0.0953). 0.105 tab aata hai jab f''(0) ka minus sign chhoot jaaye; 0.1 sirf degree-1 approximation hai; 0.09 me 2! se divide karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: f(x) = x² − 4x + 3 par [1, 3] me Rolle's theorem lagao. Guaranteed c kya hai?
questions.explanation: f(1) = 0 = f(3), aur polynomial continuous aur differentiable hai, to Rolle lagta hai. f'(c) = 2c − 4 = 0 ⇒ c = 2, jo (1, 3) me hai. 1 aur 3 endpoints hain — theorem c ko open interval (1, 3) me deta hai, yahi trap; 1.5 kisi formula se nahi aata, sirf guess hai.

questions.question: cos x ≈ 1 − x²/2 use karke cos(0.2) ka approximate value kya hai?
questions.explanation: 1 − (0.2)²/2 = 1 − 0.04/2 = 1 − 0.02 = 0.98. 0.96 tab aata hai jab /2 bhool jao; 0.8 cos x ≈ 1 − x jaisa galat linear approximation hai; 1 sirf pehla term hai.

questions.question: Inme se kis limit par L'Hôpital's rule seedha NAHI lagana chahiye?
questions.explanation: (x + 1)/(x + 2) me x = 0 rakho to 1/2 — ye 0/0 ya ∞/∞ nahi, isliye limit seedha 1/2 hai. Agar yahan rule laga do to 1/1 = 1 galat answer aata hai — form check kiye bina rule lagana trap hai. Baaki teeno indeterminate hain: sin x/x (0/0), x/eˣ (∞/∞), ln x/(x − 1) (0/0) — inpe rule valid hai.

questions.question: f(x) = x³ − 3x² − 9x + 5 ka local maximum kis x par hai aur uski value kya hai?
questions.explanation: f' = 3x² − 6x − 9 = 3(x − 3)(x + 1), critical points −1 aur 3. x = −1 ke aas-paas f' ka sign + se − hota hai ⇒ local max; f(−1) = −1 − 3 + 9 + 5 = 10. x = 3 par − se + ⇒ local min (f = −22) — max aur min ulta pehchaanne ka trap. x = 1 par f'' = 0 hai, wo critical point nahi; f = 2 arithmetic me sign ki galti hai.

questions.question: lim (x → 0) (1 − cos x)/x² kya hai?
questions.explanation: 0/0 form, L'Hôpital: sin x/(2x) — abhi bhi 0/0. Dobara: cos x/2 → 1/2. (Ya cos x ≈ 1 − x²/2 se: (x²/2)/x² = 1/2.) 0 tab aata hai jab pehle step ke baad upar sin 0 = 0 dekh ke ruk jao, ye bhoolkar ki neeche bhi 0 hai; 1 sin x/x = 1 ko pura answer maan lena hai (2 ka factor chhoot gaya); −1/2 cos ke derivative me sign ki galti hai.

questions.question: f(x) = x + eˣ one-one hai. (f⁻¹)'(1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Pehle wo x dhoondo jiske liye f(x) = 1: x + eˣ = 1 ⇒ x = 0 (0 + 1 = 1). f'(x) = 1 + eˣ, to f'(0) = 2. (f⁻¹)'(1) = 1/f'(0) = 1/2. 1/(1 + e) f' ko seedha y = 1 par evaluate karne ka trap hai; 2 reciprocal lena bhool gaye; 1 + e dono galtiyan saath me.

questions.question: eˣ ka 0 ke paas degree-3 Taylor polynomial P₃ use karke e^(0.5) ka approximate value kya milta hai?
questions.explanation: P₃(x) = 1 + x + x²/2 + x³/6. x = 0.5: 1 + 0.5 + 0.125 + 0.0208 ≈ 1.6458. 1.625 degree 2 par ruk jaana hai; 1.5 sirf linear hai; 1.6487 e^(0.5) ki asli value hai — sawaal P₃ ki value pooch raha hai, aur dono ka farak (≈ 0.003) hi remainder R₃ hai.

questions.question: √x ke 4 ke paas linear (degree-1 Taylor) approximation se √4.1 estimate karo, aur Taylor's theorem se error ki upper bound nikaalo. Kya milta hai?
lim (x → 0) (sin x − x)/x³ kya hai?
questions.explanation: Taylor se: sin x = x − x³/6 + ..., to sin x − x ≈ −x³/6, aur ratio → −1/6. L'Hôpital teen baar lagao to bhi: (cos x − 1)/(3x²) → (−sin x)/(6x) → (−cos x)/6 → −1/6. 1/6 minus sign kho dene ka trap hai; 0 tab aata hai jab sin x ≈ x le ke ruk jao — x³ wala term hi asli answer deta hai; −1/2 tab jab teesre step me 6 ki jagah 2 le lo.

weeks.title: Infinite series and power series
weeks.summary: Is week aap infinite series ka matlab partial sums se samjhoge, geometric aur harmonic series dekhoge, ratio aur root test se convergence check karoge, aur power series ka radius of convergence nikaal ke eˣ ko series ki tarah likhoge.
concepts: **Series aur partial sums**: Σ aₙ ka matlab Sₙ = a₁ + a₂ + ... + aₙ ki sequence. Agar Sₙ → S to series converge karti hai aur sum S hai; warna diverge. Series ka sawaal asal me ek sequence (Sₙ) ka sawaal hai.
**nth-term test**: Σ aₙ converge kare to aₙ → 0 zaroori hai. Isliye aₙ ↛ 0 ⇒ seedha divergent. Par ulta sach nahi: aₙ → 0 hone se convergence guarantee nahi hoti.
**Geometric series**: Σ (n = 0 se ∞) a·rⁿ = a/(1 − r) jab |r| < 1, aur |r| ≥ 1 par diverge. Jaise ek line par reflections jo har baar amplitude aadha kar dein — total response geometric sum hai.

**Harmonic aur p-series**: Σ 1/n diverge karti hai (terms → 0 hone ke bawajood — bahut dheere badhti hai, ln n jaisi). Σ 1/nᵖ converge karti hai sirf p > 1 par. Comparison test: 0 ≤ aₙ ≤ bₙ aur Σ bₙ converge ⇒ Σ aₙ bhi converge.

**Ratio test**: L = lim |aₙ₊₁/aₙ|. L < 1 ⇒ (absolutely) converge, L > 1 ⇒ diverge, L = 1 ⇒ test kuch nahi batata. **Root test**: L = lim |aₙ|^(1/n), same conclusions. Factorials ke saath ratio test, nth powers ke saath root test aasaan padta hai.

**Alternating series**: Σ (−1)ⁿbₙ, bₙ decreasing aur → 0 ⇒ converge. Σ |aₙ| bhi converge kare to **absolutely convergent**; sirf Σ aₙ kare to **conditionally**. Jaise 1 − 1/2 + 1/3 − ... conditionally converge karti hai.

**Power series**: Σ cₙ(x − a)ⁿ. Ek **radius of convergence** R hota hai: |x − a| < R par converge, |x − a| > R par diverge, endpoints alag se check karo. Ratio test se R = lim |cₙ/cₙ₊₁| (jab ye limit exist kare).
**eˣ as power series**: eˣ = Σ xⁿ/n! = 1 + x + x²/2! + x³/3! + ..., aur R = ∞ (har x par converge). Isi se e = Σ 1/n! ≈ 2.71828, aur Σ aⁿ/n! = eᵃ jaise sums seedhe pehchaan sakte ho.

example.problem: Power series Σ (n = 1 se ∞) xⁿ/(n·3ⁿ) ka radius aur interval of convergence nikalo.
steps: Endpoint x = 3: series Σ 3ⁿ/(n·3ⁿ) = Σ 1/n — harmonic, diverge.
Endpoint x = −3: series Σ (−1)ⁿ/n — alternating harmonic, converge (conditionally).

mistakes: aₙ → 0 dekh kar series ko convergent bol dena. Σ 1/n iska classic counterexample hai; nth-term test sirf divergence prove kar sakta hai.
Ratio test me L = 1 aane par conclusion nikaal dena. L = 1 par test fail hai — Σ 1/n (diverge) aur Σ 1/n² (converge) dono me L = 1 aata hai.
Radius nikaal ke endpoints check na karna. Ratio test endpoints par kuch nahi batata; wahan series ko alag se dekhna padta hai.
revision: Ratio/root: L < 1 converge, L > 1 diverge, L = 1 inconclusive.
Power series: |x − a| < R converge; endpoints alag se.

questions.question: Σ (n = 0 se ∞) 3·(1/2)ⁿ ka sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: Geometric series, a = 3 (n = 0 wala term), r = 1/2. Sum = 3/(1 − 1/2) = 6. 3 tab aata hai jab n = 1 se shuru maan ke a = 3/2 lo; |r| < 1 hai to divergence ka sawaal hi nahi.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsi series converge karti hai?
questions.explanation: Σ 1/n² p-series hai with p = 2 > 1, to converge (sum π²/6). Σ 1/n me p = 1, diverge. Σ n/(n + 1) ke terms 1 ki taraf jaate hain, 0 nahi, to nth-term test se diverge. Σ (1.1)ⁿ geometric with r > 1.

questions.question: Series Σ n²/2ⁿ par ratio test lagao. L kya hai aur conclusion kya hai?
questions.explanation: aₙ₊₁/aₙ = [(n + 1)²/2ⁿ⁺¹]·[2ⁿ/n²] = (1/2)·((n + 1)/n)² → 1/2. L = 1/2 < 1, to converge. 'L = 1' wala trap tab hota hai jab sirf (n + 1)²/n² dekho aur 2 ka factor bhool jao; L = 2 me ratio ulta le liya.

questions.question: Power series Σ (n = 0 se ∞) (x − 1)ⁿ/4ⁿ ka radius of convergence kya hai?
questions.explanation: Ye geometric series hai with r = (x − 1)/4. Converge ⇔ |x − 1|/4 < 1 ⇔ |x − 1| < 4, to R = 4 (interval (−3, 5)). R = 1/4 ratio test me coefficient ka ratio ulta lene se aata hai; R = 1 tab jab center 1 ko radius samajh lo.

questions.question: Σ (n = 0 se ∞) 2ⁿ/n! ka sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: eˣ = Σ xⁿ/n! me x = 2 rakho: sum = e² ≈ 7.389. eˣ ki series har x par converge karti hai, to ∞ galat hai. 2e tab aata hai jab 2ⁿ ko bahar ka factor 2 samajh lo.

questions.question: Power series Σ (n = 1 se ∞) n!·xⁿ/nⁿ ka radius of convergence kya hai?
questions.explanation: cₙ = n!/nⁿ. cₙ₊₁/cₙ = (n + 1)!/(n + 1)ⁿ⁺¹ · nⁿ/n! = nⁿ/(n + 1)ⁿ = 1/(1 + 1/n)ⁿ → 1/e. To |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| → |x|/e, aur converge ⇔ |x| < e, yaani R = e. 1/e wala trap ratio ki limit ko hi radius samajh lena hai — R uska reciprocal hai.

questions.question: Σ (n = 1 se ∞) (2n + 1)/(n + 5) ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: Converge karti hai, kyunki terms bounded hain
Ratio test se L < 1, isliye converge karti hai
questions.explanation: aₙ = (2n + 1)/(n + 5) → 2. Terms 0 par nahi jaate, to nth-term test se series diverge — har term lagbhag 2 jodti rahegi. 'Sum 2' term ki limit ko series ka sum samajhne ka trap hai; bounded terms convergence ke liye kaafi nahi; ratio test yahan L = 1 deta hai, jo kuch nahi batata.

questions.question: Σ (n = 1 se ∞) (2/5)ⁿ ka sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: Geometric, r = 2/5 < 1, aur pehla term (n = 1 par) 2/5 hai. Sum = (2/5)/(1 − 2/5) = (2/5)/(3/5) = 2/3. 5/3 = 1/(1 − 2/5) tab aata hai jab series ko n = 0 se shuru maan lo — starting index ka trap; 2/5 sirf pehla term hai; |r| < 1 hai, to diverge nahi karti.

questions.question: Series 1 − 1/2 + 1/3 − 1/4 + ... ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: Divergent, kyunki Σ 1/n diverge karti hai
Converge karti hai aur sum 0 hai
questions.explanation: bₙ = 1/n decreasing hai aur 0 par jaata hai, to alternating series test se series converge karti hai. Par Σ |aₙ| = Σ 1/n diverge karti hai, isliye absolutely nahi — sirf conditionally convergent. 'Divergent' absolute values wali series ko asli series samajhne ka trap hai; sum 0 nahi hai (asal me ln 2 ≈ 0.69).

questions.question: Σ (n = 1 se ∞) [n/(2n + 1)]ⁿ par root test lagao. L kya hai aur conclusion kya hai?
questions.explanation: nth power hai, to root test: |aₙ|^(1/n) = n/(2n + 1) → 1/2 < 1, isliye converge. L = 1 tab aata hai jab n/(2n + 1) ko n/n jaisa padh lo; L = 2 ratio ulta lena hai; L = 0 tab aata hai jab nth root lena bhool ke seedha aₙ ki limit (jo 0 hai) le lo.

questions.question: Σ (n = 0 se ∞) (2x)ⁿ kin x ke liye converge karti hai, aur x = 1/4 par iska sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: Geometric with r = 2x: converge ⇔ |2x| < 1 ⇔ |x| < 1/2. x = 1/4 par r = 1/2, sum = 1/(1 − 1/2) = 2. |x| < 2 me condition ulti solve hui; |x| < 1 seedha 'r ki jagah x' rakhne ka trap hai; 4/3 = 1/(1 − 1/4) tab aata hai jab r me 2 ka factor bhool jao.

questions.question: Σ (n = 1 se ∞) (n!)²/(2n)! par ratio test lagao. L kya hai aur conclusion kya hai?
questions.explanation: aₙ₊₁/aₙ = [(n + 1)!]²/(2n + 2)! · (2n)!/(n!)² = (n + 1)²/[(2n + 1)(2n + 2)]. Upar lagbhag n², neeche lagbhag 4n², to L = 1/4 < 1 ⇒ converge. 1/2 tab aata hai jab (n + 1)² ki jagah sirf (n + 1) lo, yaani square bhool jao; L = 1 factorials ko bina cancel kiye 'same size' maan lene ka guess hai; 4 ratio ulta lene ka trap hai.

questions.question: Power series Σ (n = 1 se ∞) (x − 3)ⁿ/(n·2ⁿ) ka interval of convergence kya hai (endpoints samet)?
questions.explanation: Ratio test: |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| → |x − 3|/2, to R = 2 aur centre 3: (1, 5). Endpoints alag se: x = 5 par Σ 2ⁿ/(n·2ⁿ) = Σ 1/n, jo diverge. x = 1 par Σ (−2)ⁿ/(n·2ⁿ) = Σ (−1)ⁿ/n, alternating, converge. To [1, 5). (1, 5) endpoints check na karne ka trap hai; [1, 5] harmonic series ko convergent maan leta hai; (1, 5] me dono endpoints ulat gaye.

questions.question: Ek ball 10 m ki height se giraayi jaati hai. Har bounce ke baad wo pichhli height ke 3/5 tak uthti hai. Rukne tak ball kitni total doori tay karti hai?
questions.explanation: Pehla girna 10 m. Phir har bounce me upar aur neeche dono: 2 × (6 + 3.6 + 2.16 + ...) = 2 × 6/(1 − 3/5) = 2 × 15 = 30 m. Total = 10 + 30 = 40 m. 25 m = 10/(1 − 3/5) sirf neeche ki doori hai (upar jaana bhool gaye); 50 m tab aata hai jab pehle 10 m ko bhi double gin lo; 30 m pehla girna chhod deta hai.

questions.question: Σ (n = 0 se ∞) (n + 1)/n! ka sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: Todo: Σ n/n! + Σ 1/n!. Doosra = e. Pehle me n = 0 wala term 0 hai, aur n ≥ 1 ke liye n/n! = 1/(n − 1)!, to Σ (n ≥ 1) 1/(n − 1)! = 1 + 1 + 1/2! + ... = e. Total 2e. e tab aata hai jab ek hissa bhool jao; e + 1 tab jab Σ n/n! ko sirf 1 maan lo; e² sum ko product samajhne ka trap hai.

weeks.title: Riemann sums and the definite integral
weeks.summary: Is week aap area ko chhote rectangles ke sum (Riemann sum) se approximate karoge, definite integral ko uski limit ki tarah define karoge, fundamental theorem of calculus se integral nikaloge, aur substitution aur integration by parts ki techniques seekhoge.
concepts: **Riemann sum**: [a, b] ko n barabar tukdon me kaato, Δx = (b − a)/n. Har tukde me ek point xᵢ* chuno aur Σ f(xᵢ*)Δx lo. Left endpoint, right endpoint ya midpoint — teeno common choices. Increasing f ke liye left sum kam aur right sum zyada estimate deta hai.
**Definite integral**: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = lim (n → ∞) Σ f(xᵢ*)Δx. Ye **signed area** hai — x-axis ke upar wala area +, neeche wala −. Continuous function ka integral hamesha exist karta hai.

**Properties**: linearity ∫(αf + βg) = α∫f + β∫g; additivity: (a se c tak ka integral) = (a se b tak) + (b se c tak); limits ulti karo to sign badal jaata hai; ∫ₐᵃ f dx = 0. Average value of f on [a, b] = (1/(b − a))∫ₐᵇ f dx — jaise ek signal ka DC (average) level.
**FTC part 1**: F(x) = ∫ₐˣ f(t) dt ho to F'(x) = f(x). Upper limit g(x) ho to chain rule: d/dx ∫ₐ^g(x) f(t) dt = f(g(x))·g'(x). Integration aur differentiation ek doosre ko undo karte hain.
**FTC part 2**: agar F' = f (F ek antiderivative hai), to ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a). Ab limit of sums ki jagah sirf antiderivative chahiye. Physics me: charge q = ∫ i dt, energy = ∫ p dt.
**Substitution**: ∫ f(g(x))g'(x) dx me u = g(x), du = g'(x)dx. Definite integral me limits bhi badlo: x = a ⇒ u = g(a), x = b ⇒ u = g(b). Phir wapas x me jaane ki zaroorat nahi.

**Integration by parts**: ∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du (product rule ka ulta). u wo chuno jo differentiate karke simple ho jaaye — order LIATE: Log, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential. Definite me: [uv]ₐᵇ − ∫ₐᵇ v du.

steps: Product of algebraic (x) aur exponential (eˣ) — by parts. LIATE se u = x, dv = eˣ dx.
∫ x eˣ dx = x eˣ − ∫ eˣ dx = x eˣ − eˣ = eˣ(x − 1).
Sanity check: [0, 1] par x eˣ positive hai aur max value e ≈ 2.7, to answer 0 aur 2.7 ke beech hona chahiye ✓.

mistakes: Substitution ke baad purani x-limits hi rakh dena. u = x² + 1 lo to x = 0 → u = 1 aur x = 2 → u = 5 — limits bhi convert karo.
FTC part 1 me chain rule bhool jaana: d/dx ∫₀^(x²) cos t dt = cos(x²)·2x, sirf cos(x²) nahi.
F(b) − F(a) me sirf F(b) lena, ya lower limit par F ko 0 maan lena. ln, cos jaise functions lower limit par 0 nahi hote.
revision: ∫ₐᵇ f dx = lim Σ f(xᵢ*)Δx, Δx = (b − a)/n.
By parts: ∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du (LIATE).

questions.question: ∫₁³ (2x + 1) dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Antiderivative F(x) = x² + x. F(3) − F(1) = (9 + 3) − (1 + 1) = 12 − 2 = 10. 12 sirf F(3) hai — lower limit ghatana bhool gaye; 8 me +1 term ka integral (x) chhoot gaya.

questions.question: f(x) = x² ke liye [0, 2] par n = 4 barabar tukdon ke saath left Riemann sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: Δx = 0.5, left endpoints 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5. Sum = (0 + 0.25 + 1 + 2.25) × 0.5 = 3.5 × 0.5 = 1.75. 3.75 right Riemann sum hai, 2.67 exact integral 8/3 hai, aur 3.5 me Δx se multiply karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: d/dx ∫₀^(x²) cos t dt kya hai?
questions.explanation: FTC part 1 + chain rule: upper limit g(x) = x², to answer cos(g(x))·g'(x) = 2x cos(x²). cos(x²) me chain rule ka 2x bhool gaye. sin(x²) to integral ki value hai, uska derivative nahi.

questions.question: ∫₀² x(x² + 1)³ dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: u = x² + 1, du = 2x dx, to x dx = du/2. Limits: x = 0 → u = 1, x = 2 → u = 5. Integral = (1/2)∫₁⁵ u³ du = (1/2)·(625 − 1)/4 = 624/8 = 78. 156 me du/2 wala 1/2 bhool gaye — substitution ka sabse common trap.

questions.question: Ek wire me current i(t) = 6t² mA hai (t second me). t = 0 se t = 2 s tak kitna charge q = ∫ i dt guzra?
questions.explanation: q = ∫₀² 6t² dt = [2t³]₀² = 16 mC. 24 mC to i(2) = 24 mA ko charge samajh lena hai (integral ki jagah value); 8 mC me 6/3 = 2 ka factor chhoot gaya (sirf t³).

questions.question: ∫₁ᵉ ln x dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: By parts: u = ln x, dv = dx ⇒ du = dx/x, v = x. ∫ ln x dx = x ln x − ∫ 1 dx = x ln x − x. [x ln x − x]₁ᵉ = (e − e) − (0 − 1) = 1. '0' sirf F(e) hai — lower limit par F(1) = −1 ghatana bhool gaye. 'e' tab aata hai jab −∫ v du wala hissa chhod do (sirf [x ln x]), aur e − 1 to wahi ∫₁ᵉ 1 dx hai jo ghatana tha.

questions.question: ∫₀¹ (3x² + 2x) dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Antiderivative F(x) = x³ + x². F(1) − F(0) = (1 + 1) − 0 = 2. 5 = integrand ki x = 1 par value (3 + 2) — integrate karna hi bhool gaye, yahi trap; 3 tab aata hai jab 3x² ka integral 3x³ le lo aur doosra term chhod do; 1 tab jab ek term chhoot jaaye.

questions.question: ∫₁⁴ f(x) dx = 7 aur ∫₁² f(x) dx = 3 hai. ∫₄² f(x) dx kya hai?
questions.explanation: Additivity: ∫₁⁴ = ∫₁² + ∫₂⁴ ⇒ ∫₂⁴ = 7 − 3 = 4. Limits ulti karne se sign badalta hai: ∫₄² = −4. 4 sign badalna bhool jaane ka trap hai; 10 aur −10 tab aate hain jab 7 aur 3 ko ghatane ki jagah jod do.

questions.question: f(x) = x² ki [0, 3] par average value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Average = (1/(3 − 0))∫₀³ x² dx = (1/3)(27/3) = (1/3)(9) = 3. 9 sirf integral hai, (b − a) se divide nahi kiya; 4.5 = (f(0) + f(3))/2 endpoints ka average hai — curve ke liye ye average value nahi hota, yahi trap.

questions.question: f(x) = 1/x ke liye [1, 3] par n = 4 barabar tukdon ke saath right Riemann sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: Δx = (3 − 1)/4 = 0.5, right endpoints 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3. Sum = 0.5(1/1.5 + 1/2 + 1/2.5 + 1/3) = 0.5(0.667 + 0.5 + 0.4 + 0.333) = 0.5 × 1.9 = 0.95. 1/x decreasing hai, to right sum asli area (ln 3 ≈ 1.10) se kam aata hai. 1.28 left sum hai; 1.90 me Δx se multiply bhool gaye; 1.10 exact integral hai, Riemann sum nahi.

questions.question: F(x) = ∫₁ˣ (t² + 1) dt. F'(2) aur F(1) kramshah kya hain?
questions.explanation: FTC part 1: F'(x) = x² + 1, to F'(2) = 5. F(1) = ∫₁¹ = 0 (same limits). 10/3 = F(2) hai, F'(2) nahi — derivative aur integral mix karne ka trap; 'F(1) = 2' integrand ko 1 par rakh dene se aata hai; 4 me +1 chhoot gaya.

questions.question: G(x) = ∫_(2x)^(x³) dt/(1 + t²) ho to G'(1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Dono limits variable hain: G'(x) = f(x³)·3x² − f(2x)·2, jahan f(t) = 1/(1 + t²). x = 1: (1/2)·3 − (1/5)·2 = 3/2 − 2/5 = 11/10. 3/10 = 1/2 − 1/5 chain rule ke factors (3x² aur 2) bhoolne ka trap hai; 3/2 sirf upper limit wala hissa hai; 19/10 lower limit wale term ka minus sign chhodne se aata hai.

questions.question: ∫₁² x/(x² + 1) dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: u = x² + 1, du = 2x dx, to x dx = du/2. Limits: x = 1 ⇒ u = 2, x = 2 ⇒ u = 5. Integral = (1/2)∫₂⁵ du/u = (1/2)(ln 5 − ln 2) = (1/2) ln(5/2). ln(5/2) me 1/2 factor gaayab hai; (1/2) ln 2 tab aata hai jab purani x-limits 1 aur 2 hi u me rakh do — limits convert na karne ka trap; 2 ln(5/2) me du/2 ko 2du padh liya.

questions.question: ∫₀¹ x eˣ dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: By parts: u = x (algebraic), dv = eˣ dx ⇒ du = dx, v = eˣ. ∫ = [x eˣ]₀¹ − ∫₀¹ eˣ dx = e − (e − 1) = 1. 2e − 1 formula me minus ki jagah plus (uv + ∫v du) lagane ka trap hai; e − 1 sirf ∫eˣ hai; e sirf uv wala hissa hai.

questions.question: lim (n → ∞) Σ (i = 1 se n) (2/n)·(1 + 2i/n)² ki value kya hai? (Ise ek definite integral ki tarah pehchaano.)
questions.explanation: Δx = 2/n aur xᵢ = 1 + 2i/n: ye [1, 3] par f(x) = x² ka right Riemann sum hai. Limit = ∫₁³ x² dx = (27 − 1)/3 = 26/3. 13/3 tab aata hai jab Δx = 2/n ki jagah 1/n le lo; 8/3 = ∫₀² x² dx, jo interval ko [0, 2] samajhne ka trap hai; 9 = ∫₀³ x² dx, lower limit 1 bhool gaye.

weeks.title: Applications of integration and improper integrals
weeks.summary: Is week aap integral se area between curves, solids of revolution ka volume aur curve ki arc length nikaloge, infinite limits wale improper integrals handle karoge, aur logarithm ko ek integral ki tarah define karke uski properties samjhoge.
concepts: **Area between curves**: [a, b] par f(x) ≥ g(x) ho to area = ∫ₐᵇ [f(x) − g(x)] dx (upar wala − neeche wala). Limits aksar curves ke intersection points hote hain — pehle f(x) = g(x) solve karo.

**Volume of revolution (disc method)**: y = f(x), a ≤ x ≤ b ko x-axis ke around ghumao to V = π∫ₐᵇ [f(x)]² dx — har slice radius f(x) wali disc hai. Beech me hole ho (**washer**) to V = π∫ₐᵇ (R² − r²) dx.

**Arc length**: y = f(x), a se b tak curve ki length L = ∫ₐᵇ √(1 + [f'(x)]²) dx. Chhote tukde ki length √(dx² + dy²) se ye formula aata hai. Bahut kam functions ke liye ye integral seedha nikalta hai, isliye questions aksar specially chune hote hain.
**Improper integral (type 1, infinite limit)**: ∫ₐ^∞ f dx = lim (b → ∞) ∫ₐᵇ f dx. Limit finite ho to converge, warna diverge. Key result: ∫₁^∞ dx/xᵖ converge ⇔ p > 1 (tab value 1/(p − 1)).

**Improper integral (type 2, unbounded integrand)**: endpoint par f infinite ho, jaise ∫₀¹ dx/√x, to ∫₀¹ = lim (ε → 0⁺) ∫_ε¹. Key result: ∫₀¹ dx/xᵖ converge ⇔ p < 1. Dhyan do: ∫₋₁¹ dx/x² ko seedha F(1) − F(−1) se karna galat hai — beech me x = 0 par blow-up hai.

**Electronics me improper integrals**: discharge current i(t) = (V₀/R)e^(−t/RC) ka total charge ∫₀^∞ i dt = CV₀, aur resistor me total energy ∫₀^∞ i²R dt = CV₀²/2 — dono finite, kyunki exponential tezi se 0 jaata hai.
**Logarithm as an integral**: ln x = ∫₁ˣ dt/t (x > 0). Isse seedha milta hai (ln x)' = 1/x, ln 1 = 0, aur ln(ab) = ln a + ln b, ln(aʳ) = r ln a. e wo number hai jiske liye ∫₁ᵉ dt/t = 1.

example.problem: 100 μF capacitor 10 V se 1 kΩ resistor ke through discharge hota hai: i(t) = (V₀/R)e^(−t/RC). Resistor me total kitni energy E = ∫₀^∞ i²R dt dissipate hogi?
steps: b → ∞ par e^(−2b/RC) → 0, to improper integral = RC/2 (converge karta hai).
E = (V₀²/R)·(RC/2) = CV₀²/2 — R cancel ho gaya!
Answer: **E = 5 mJ**, jo exactly capacitor me shuru me stored energy hai.

mistakes: Area me curves ka order ulta lena aur negative area likh dena. Pehle check karo kaunsa curve upar hai, ya |f − g| ka integral lo.
Disc method me f(x)² ki jagah f(x) integrate kar dena. Disc ka area πr² hai, isliye radius ka square chahiye.

Improper integral ko normal integral ki tarah solve karna jab integrand beech me blow up kare. ∫₋₁¹ dx/x² ka 'answer −2' aata hai jo positive function ke liye absurd hai — asal me ye diverge karta hai.
revision: ∫₁^∞ dx/xᵖ converges ⇔ p > 1; ∫₀¹ dx/xᵖ converges ⇔ p < 1.

questions.question: Curves y = x aur y = x² ke beech, x = 0 se x = 1 tak ka area kya hai?
questions.explanation: [0, 1] par x ≥ x², to area = ∫₀¹ (x − x²) dx = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6. 1/2 sirf y = x ke neeche ka area hai aur 1/3 sirf y = x² ke neeche ka; 5/6 tab aata hai jab dono areas ko ghatane ki jagah jod do.

questions.question: ∫₁^∞ dx/x² ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∫₁ᵇ x⁻² dx = [−1/x]₁ᵇ = 1 − 1/b → 1 jab b → ∞. p = 2 > 1, to converge. 'Diverge' wala trap ye sochna hai ki infinite interval par area hamesha infinite hota hai — par 1/x² itni tezi se girta hai ki total finite rehta hai.

questions.question: y = √x, 0 ≤ x ≤ 4 ko x-axis ke around ghumane se bane solid ka volume kya hai?
questions.explanation: Disc method: V = π∫₀⁴ (√x)² dx = π∫₀⁴ x dx = π·16/2 = 8π. 16π/3 tab aata hai jab square kiye bina π∫√x dx kar do (π·(2/3)·8); 16π me x²/2 ka 1/2 bhool gaye.

questions.question: Curve y = (2/3)x^(3/2) ki x = 0 se x = 3 tak arc length kya hai?
questions.explanation: y' = x^(1/2), to 1 + y'² = 1 + x. L = ∫₀³ √(1 + x) dx = (2/3)[(1 + x)^(3/2)]₀³ = (2/3)(8 − 1) = 14/3. 16/3 me lower limit ka (2/3)·1 ghatana bhool gaye; 3 to sirf horizontal distance hai — curve ki length usse zyada honi hi chahiye.

questions.question: Improper integral ∫₀¹ dx/√x ke baare me kya sahi hai?
questions.explanation: x = 0 par integrand unbounded hai. ∫_ε¹ x^(−1/2) dx = [2√x]_ε¹ = 2 − 2√ε → 2 jab ε → 0⁺. p = 1/2 < 1, to converge. 'Diverge' wala trap hai blow-up dekh ke ruk jaana; 1/2 power rule me exponent se multiply karne par aata hai.

questions.question: R = 1 kΩ, C = 20 μF, V₀ = 50 V. Discharge me resistor ki total energy E = ∫₀^∞ (V₀²/R)e^(−2t/(RC)) dt kitni hai?
questions.explanation: ∫₀^∞ e^(−2t/(RC)) dt = RC/2. To E = (V₀²/R)(RC/2) = CV₀²/2 = (1/2)(20 × 10⁻⁶)(2500) = 0.025 J = 25 mJ. 50 mJ me exponent ka 2 bhool gaye (integral RC le liya), jo CV₀² deta hai.

questions.question: Line y = 9 aur parabola y = x² ke beech band region ka area kya hai?
questions.explanation: Intersection: x² = 9 ⇒ x = ±3. Upar y = 9, neeche y = x². Area = ∫₋₃³ (9 − x²) dx = [9x − x³/3]₋₃³ = 18 − (−18) = 36. 18 sirf aadha (0 se 3) hai; 72 tab aata hai jab ghataane ki jagah jod do (9 + x²); 54 = ∫₋₃³ 9 dx poora rectangle hai — parabola ke neeche ka hissa ghataya hi nahi.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa improper integral converge karta hai?
questions.explanation: ∫₀¹ dx/xᵖ tab converge karta hai jab p < 1; yahan p = 1/3, to converge (value 3/2). ∫₁^∞ dx/xᵖ ke liye p > 1 chahiye — √x (p = 1/2) aur x (p = 1) dono fail. ∫₀¹ dx/x² me p = 2, jo 0 ke paas diverge karta hai. Do types ki conditions (p > 1 aur p < 1) ko mix karna yahan ka trap hai.

questions.question: ln x = ∫₁ˣ dt/t use karke ∫₁⁸ dt/t − ∫₁² dt/t ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: ln 8 − ln 2 = ln(8/2) = ln 4. (Ya seedha ∫₂⁸ dt/t = ln 4.) ln 6 = ln(8 − 2), jo log ke rule ko galat lagana hai — yahi trap; ln 16 me minus ko plus maan liya (ln 8 + ln 2); 6 limits ko hi ghata dena hai.

questions.question: y = x², 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 ko x-axis ke around ghumane se bane solid ka volume kya hai?
questions.explanation: Disc method: V = π∫₀¹ (x²)² dx = π∫₀¹ x⁴ dx = π/5. π/3 = π∫x² dx, jisme radius ka square lena bhool gaye — sabse common trap; π/2 aur 2π/5 integration me power galat badhane se aate hain.

questions.question: R = 2 kΩ, C = 47 μF, V₀ = 12 V. Discharge current i(t) = (V₀/R)e^(−t/RC) se total charge ∫₀^∞ i dt kitna guzarta hai?
questions.explanation: ∫₀^∞ (V₀/R)e^(−t/RC) dt = (V₀/R)·RC = CV₀ = 47 μF × 12 V = 564 μC. R cancel ho jaata hai. 6 mC tab aata hai jab starting current V₀/R = 6 mA ko 1 second se multiply kar do — current constant nahi, exponentially girta hai, yahi trap; 282 μC = CV₀/2 energy wale formula se confuse karna hai; 47 μC me V₀ se multiply bhool gaye.

questions.question: Curves y = x² aur y = 2x + 3 ke beech band region ka area kya hai?
questions.explanation: Intersection: x² = 2x + 3 ⇒ (x − 3)(x + 1) = 0 ⇒ x = −1, 3. Beech me line upar hai (jaise x = 0 par 3 > 0). Area = ∫₋₁³ (2x + 3 − x²) dx = [x² + 3x − x³/3]₋₁³ = 9 − (−5/3) = 32/3. −32/3 curves ka order ulta lene ka trap hai — area negative nahi ho sakta; 9 sirf upper limit par F ki value hai, F(−1) ghataya nahi; 64/3 area ko galti se double kar deta hai.

questions.question: y = x aur y = x² ke beech (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) ka region x-axis ke around ghumaya jaata hai. Solid ka volume kya hai?
questions.explanation: Washer: outer radius R = x, inner r = x². V = π∫₀¹ (x² − x⁴) dx = π(1/3 − 1/5) = 2π/15. π/30 = π∫(x − x²)² dx, yaani (R − r)² lena — washer me R² − r² hota hai, (R − r)² nahi, yahi trap; π/6 = π × area (1/6), square lena hi bhool gaye; π/15 sahi answer ka aadha hai.

questions.question: ∫₋₁⁸ dx/x^(1/3) ke baare me kya sahi hai?
questions.explanation: x = 0 par integrand blow up karta hai, to do tukde: ∫₋₁⁰ + ∫₀⁸. Antiderivative (3/2)x^(2/3), aur p = 1/3 < 1, to dono tukde converge. ∫₀⁸ = (3/2)(4) = 6, ∫₋₁⁰ = 0 − (3/2)(1) = −1.5. Total 4.5. 'Diverge' har blow-up ko divergence samajhne ka trap hai; 7.5 me negative hissa (x < 0 par integrand negative hai) ka sign galat liya; 6 sirf ek tukda hai.

questions.question: Curve y = x^(3/2) ki x = 0 se x = 4/3 tak arc length kya hai?
questions.explanation: y' = (3/2)x^(1/2), to 1 + (y')² = 1 + 9x/4. L = ∫₀^(4/3) √(1 + 9x/4) dx. u = 1 + 9x/4, dx = (4/9)du, aur u 1 se 4 tak. L = (4/9)·(2/3)[u^(3/2)]₁⁴ = (8/27)(8 − 1) = 56/27. 64/27 lower limit (u = 1) wala term bhoolne ka trap hai; 8/27 sirf constant factor hai; 14/3 me substitution ka (4/9) factor chhoot gaya.

weeks.title: Complex numbers, Euler's formula and phasors
weeks.summary: Is week aap complex numbers ka arithmetic, complex plane, polar form aur Euler's formula seekhoge, roots of unity nikaloge, aur dekhoge ki same frequency ke sinusoids ko phasors se kaise jodte hain.
concepts: **Complex number**: z = a + jb, jahan j² = −1 (electronics me i ki jagah j likhte hain kyunki i current ke liye hai). Re(z) = a, Im(z) = b. Conjugate z̄ = a − jb, aur z·z̄ = a² + b² (hamesha real, ≥ 0).

**Arithmetic**: add/subtract component-wise. Multiply normal brackets ki tarah aur j² = −1 rakho. Divide karne ke liye upar-neeche denominator ke conjugate se multiply karo: (a + jb)/(c + jd) = (a + jb)(c − jd)/(c² + d²).

**Complex plane aur polar form**: z = a + jb point (a, b) hai. Modulus r = |z| = √(a² + b²), argument θ jahan cos θ = a/r, sin θ = b/r. z = r(cos θ + j sin θ) = r∠θ. Quadrant dhyan se: −1 + j√3 ka argument 120° hai, calculator ka tan⁻¹(−√3) = −60° nahi.

**Euler's formula**: e^(jθ) = cos θ + j sin θ, to z = r·e^(jθ). Multiply: moduli multiply, angles add. Divide: moduli divide, angles subtract. **De Moivre**: (r e^(jθ))ⁿ = rⁿ e^(jnθ) — badi powers ek line me.

**Trig identities from Euler**: cos θ = (e^(jθ) + e^(−jθ))/2, sin θ = (e^(jθ) − e^(−jθ))/(2j). e^(j(A + B)) = e^(jA)e^(jB) ke real aur imaginary parts compare karo to cos(A + B) aur sin(A + B) ke formulas khud nikal aate hain.

**Roots of unity**: zⁿ = 1 ke exactly n roots hain: e^(j2πk/n), k = 0, 1, ..., n − 1 — unit circle par barabar 360°/n ki doori par. Inka sum 0 hota hai (n ≥ 2). zⁿ = w ke roots ke liye |w|^(1/n) radius aur arg/n se shuru karke 360°/n jodte jao.

**Sinusoids aur phasors**: A cos(ωt + φ) = Re{A e^(jφ) e^(jωt)}. Same ω wale sinusoids ke liye e^(jωt) common hai, to sirf **phasor** A∠φ track karo. Do sinusoids jodne ke liye phasors complex numbers ki tarah jodo, phir wapas magnitude aur angle lo. sin ωt = cos(ωt − 90°) yaad rakho.

example.problem: v(t) = 3 cos(ωt) + 4 sin(ωt) ko ek single sinusoid A cos(ωt + φ) ki form me likho.
steps: 4 sin(ωt) = 4 cos(ωt − 90°), to phasors hain 3∠0° aur 4∠−90°.
Angle: point (3, −4) fourth quadrant me hai, φ = −tan⁻¹(4/3) ≈ −53.13°.
Check: 5 cos(ωt − 53.13°) = 5[cos ωt·(0.6) + sin ωt·(0.8)] = 3 cos ωt + 4 sin ωt ✓.

mistakes: j² = +1 le lena ya multiply karte waqt j² wala term bhool jaana. Har j·j ko −1 me badlo.
Argument ke liye seedha tan⁻¹(b/a) lena. a < 0 ho to point second/third quadrant me hai, aur angle me 180° jodna/ghatana padta hai.
Amplitudes ko seedha jod dena (3 + 4 = 7). Alag phase wale sinusoids vectors ki tarah judte hain, numbers ki tarah nahi.
revision: z = r e^(jθ) = r(cos θ + j sin θ).
Multiply: r₁r₂, θ₁ + θ₂; power: rⁿ, nθ.
zⁿ = 1 ke roots: e^(j2πk/n), k = 0 ... n − 1, sum 0.
A cos(ωt + φ) ↔ phasor A∠φ; sin ωt = cos(ωt − 90°).

questions.question: (2 + 3j)(1 − j) kya hai?
questions.explanation: 2·1 + 2·(−j) + 3j·1 + 3j·(−j) = 2 − 2j + 3j − 3j² = 2 + j + 3 = 5 + j. −1 + j tab aata hai jab j² = +1 le lo (2 + j − 3); 2 − 3j me real-real aur imaginary-imaginary ko alag-alag multiply kar diya.

questions.question: z = −1 + j√3 ka modulus aur argument kya hai?
questions.explanation: |z| = √(1 + 3) = 2. Point (−1, √3) second quadrant me hai, cos θ = −1/2, sin θ = √3/2 ⇒ θ = 120°. −60° calculator ka tan⁻¹(√3/(−1)) hai jo quadrant ignore karta hai; 4 me square root lena bhool gaye.

questions.question: (1 + j)⁸ kya hai?
questions.explanation: 1 + j = √2·e^(jπ/4). De Moivre: (√2)⁸·e^(j8π/4) = 16·e^(j2π) = 16. 256 tab aata hai jab modulus 2 maan lo (2⁸); −16 me angle 2π ki jagah π le liya.

questions.question: (3 + 4j)/(1 + 2j) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Conjugate (1 − 2j) se multiply: (3 + 4j)(1 − 2j)/(1 + 4) = (3 − 6j + 4j + 8)/5 = (11 − 2j)/5 = 2.2 − 0.4j. 3 + 2j component-wise divide karne se aata hai (3/1, 4/2); −1 + 2j tab jab conjugate ki jagah (1 + 2j) se hi multiply kar do.

questions.question: Equation z⁴ = 16 ke saare complex roots kaunse hain?
questions.explanation: 16 = 16e^(j0), to roots 16^(1/4)·e^(j2πk/4) = 2e^(jkπ/2), k = 0, 1, 2, 3: yaani 2, 2j, −2, −2j. 'Sirf 2 aur −2' real roots tak ruk jaana hai — degree 4 ke 4 roots hote hain. Last option me roots 45° ki doori par liye, jo 8th roots ka pattern hai.

questions.question: v(t) = 5 cos(ωt) + 5 cos(ωt + 90°) ko ek single sinusoid ki form me likho.
